title: ws_risk orphan-close has no positive-evidence requirement; an empty-but-successful get_positions zero-PnL-closes live trades
evidence: The single reconcile authority (ws_risk) calls `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions(..., enabled=submit_orders, position_error=last_position_error)`. Its only guard against the known 'empty fetch = mass deletion' class is `position_error` being non-empty. But `_safe_raw_positions` (event_demo.py:2120) returns `([], '')` — empty list, NO error — both when there are genuinely no positions AND when Bybit returns a successful (retCode 0) response with an empty `result.list` during a partial venue degradation. `_call` only raises on a non-zero retCode or a transport exception; a 200/retCode-0 with an erroneously-empty list passes the guard. `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions` then closes EVERY open trade whose symbol is absent (line 1418, hard-wired `require_evidence=False`), and `_orphan_close_trade_row` with require_evidence=False writes a `bybit_position_missing` close even when `_orphan_close_pnl_backfill` finds no closure record (backfill returns {} -> zero-PnL close, line 1441 only blocks on require_evidence=True which this path never sets). The docstring at lines 1410-1417 claims the fail-closed require_evidence=True path protects 'the cycle path' — but that is a DIFFERENT function; the ws_risk authority here is always require_evidence=False.
impact: On a Bybit-side empty-but-200 positions response (observed class of API degradation), ws_risk can mass-close the live ledger to zero-PnL `bybit_position_missing` rows while the positions are still open at the venue — corrupting the ledger, dropping the true trade outcomes, and clearing the in-memory open_trades so stops stop being evaluated for those (still-open) positions until re-adoption. This is the exact prior-CRITICAL empty-fetch class, only narrowed (not eliminated) by the transport-error guard.
proposed_fix: Make the ws_risk orphan-close fail-closed like the cycle path: require POSITIVE closure evidence (require_evidence=True) before writing a close, so a still-open position with no closed-PnL record stays OPEN. Additionally treat an empty-list positions response as suspect when open_trades is non-empty (require N consecutive empty reads, or cross-check get_closed_pnl) before acting.

verdict.reasoning: Traced the concrete triggering path and confirmed it with existing tests. (1) bybit.py `_call` (lines 694-716) raises ONLY on non-zero retCode or a transport exception; a 200/retCode-0 payload with an empty `result.list` is passed through unmodified, so `get_positions` (bybit.py:499-500) returns `[]`. (2) `_safe_raw_positions` (event_demo.py:2120-2126) therefore returns `([], "")` — empty list, NO error — for both the genuine no-positions case AND a retCode-0-empty-list degradation. (3) In ws_risk `rest_reconcile` (lines 1296-1345), with the default config (`reconcile_prefetch_enabled=False`, line 118), the empty read is NOT caught by `if error:` (line 1313, error is ""), so line 1319 clears `last_position_error=""` and line 1329 (the `else`/replace branch, because prefetch is off) sets `positions_by_symbol = {}` — a full REPLACE, clobbering any WS-maintained positions. (4) Line 1345 then calls `reconcile_positions` → `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions(..., position_error="")`; the only guard (line 1401 `if position_error:`) passes, and every open trade absent from `{}` hits `_orphan_close_trade_row(..., require_evidence=False)` (line 1419, hard-wired, no knob — confirmed the ws_risk path is always require_evidence=False, unlike the cycle path which has the `orphan_close_require_evidence=True` default at event_demo.py:92). (5) `_orphan_close_pnl_backfill` queries get_closed_pnl; for a still-open position there is no closure record → backfill `{}` → `require_evidence and not backfill` = `False and ...` = False (line 1441) → a zero-PnL `bybit_position_missing` close is written and `open_trades` is cleared. This exact behavior is asserted by `test_risk_reconciler_closes_orphan_when_position_missing` (tests/test_liquidity_migration_event_demo_exits.py:1309-1325): position_error="", empty positions → close fires. The prior 2026-05-29 CRITICAL audit fixed this empty-fetch class on the cycle path (require_evidence) and the WS-cache path, but per the audit memory deliberately "kept grace-protected behavior" on the risk path — and the grace window only gates the OPPOSITE (adopt) direction (the docstring at lines 1413-1415 admits this), so the ws_risk orphan-close has NO evidence requirement and NO grace; its sole defense is the `position_error` guard, which the retCode-0-empty case bypasses. The trigger (retCode-0 with an empty settleCoin list while positions are open) is a real exchange degradation class (backend lag / settleCoin index staleness / region failover), rarer than a transport error but genuine. Severity is high not critical: the live account is demo-only (REAL_MONEY default off), so the immediate impact is corruption of the forward-demo arbiter ledger (false zero-PnL closes, lost trade outcomes, and cleared open_trades so stops stop being evaluated until re-adoption), with the real-money path being a latent catastrophic case — matching the prior C1 framing.
verdict.fix_notes: The proposed `require_evidence=True` on the ws_risk path is directionally correct (it stops the zero-PnL false-close: with no closed-PnL record the trade stays OPEN) but is NOT side-effect-free. ws_risk is the single reconcile authority for the netted shared account (3 sleeves), and the WS `on_position_message` size=0 path (ws_risk.py:649-668) calls reconcile_positions the instant the venue reports a position vanished. Bybit's get_closed_pnl endpoint lags the position stream by seconds, so a require_evidence=True gate would, on a genuine close, leave the (truly-gone) position lingering as `open` in open_trades until a later cycle indexes the closed-PnL record — delaying the close, keeping the symbol reserved, and blocking sibling sleeves from re-using it on the netted account. That is the very tradeoff the owner avoided when they "kept grace-protected behavior" on the risk path. The better, more targeted fix is the auditor's SECONDARY proposal: treat an empty positions snapshot as SUSPECT when open_trades is non-empty — require N consecutive empty reads (a counter on EngineState, reset on any non-empty read) and/or a same-cycle cross-check (e.g. a per-symbol get_positions or get_closed_pnl confirmation) before clobbering positions_by_symbol to {} / mass-closing. Concretely: in rest_reconcile, when `snapshot_positions` is empty AND `open_trades` is non-empty AND no prior error, do NOT replace positions_by_symbol and skip the orphan reconcile for that pass (set a soft suspicion flag), only acting once the empty result repeats across consecutive reconcile passes. This kills the mass-false-close (the EXEC-2 trigger) without changing the evidence semantics of a normal single-symbol WS-size-0 close, so legitimate orphan-closes stay prompt. If require_evidence=True is also adopted, scope it behind the same config knob as the cycle path (orphan_close_require_evidence) rather than hard-coding, and verify the closed-PnL lag does not strand positions on the shared ledger. Either fix needs a regression test asserting that an empty-but-no-error positions read with non-empty open_trades does NOT orphan-close on a single pass.

title: ws_risk orphan-close fails OPEN only on an exception, not on a successful-but-empty get_positions; a retCode=0 empty list mass-closes the whole ledger
evidence: The C1 'empty fetch == mass deletion' protection is built entirely on `position_error` being non-empty. `_safe_raw_positions` only sets the error string inside `except` — but BybitPrivateClient.get_positions returns `payload.get('result',{}).get('list',[])` and `_call` only raises on retCode!=0. A retCode=0 response that returns an empty list (a real Bybit behaviour mode: wrong/missing settleCoin scoping, a transient backend that returns an empty page with retCode=0, or a >200-position account where the un-paginated single-page call returns an unexpected empty/partial page) yields `([], '')`. On the ws_risk path `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions` runs with require_evidence=False, so EVERY open ledger trade whose symbol is absent from `position_by_symbol` is orphan-closed; `_orphan_close_pnl_backfill` returning {} does NOT block the close (it only blocks on the cycle path where require_evidence=True). Net: one successful-but-empty positions read on the shared ws_risk authority closes all three sleeves' open trades into the ledger at zero/fabricated PnL.
impact: Ledger corruption + spurious mass reduce-only closes on the live shared account (the single reconcile authority). On a real-money toggle this dumps every open position at market on a single benign-looking empty API response. This is the same class as the known prior CRITICAL false-orphan-close, but the residual trigger (empty list with retCode=0) is not guarded — only the raised-exception trigger is.
proposed_fix: Treat a zero-length positions list as a DISTRUSTED snapshot when open ledger trades exist: in `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions` / `reconcile_positions`, if `position_by_symbol` is empty AND open_trades is non-empty AND this is a freshly-fetched REST snapshot (not the WS-maintained map), require positive closure evidence (require_evidence=True semantics) or skip the pass and surface a sentinel error. Alternatively, in `_safe_raw_positions`, validate the response shape (retCode/retMsg present) and return an error when the API returns an empty list while a non-empty list was expected by a recent prior snapshot.

verdict.reasoning: Traced the full concrete path on the ws_risk reconcile authority. (1) BybitPrivateClient.get_positions (bybit.py:493-500) returns payload['result']['list'] directly, single-page/un-paginated; _call (bybit.py:694-716) raises ONLY on retCode!=0, so a retCode=0 response with an empty list returns [] with no exception. (2) _safe_raw_positions (event_demo.py:2120-2126) therefore returns ([], "") — empty list, EMPTY error string. (3) ws_risk.bootstrap (516-522) and rest_reconcile (1312-1329) set last_position_error="" and positions_by_symbol={} (in the non-prefetch/default path positions_by_symbol = snapshot_positions overwrites the WS-maintained map), then call reconcile_positions(write=True) (533/1345). (4) reconcile_positions (1278-1285) passes position_by_symbol={} and position_error="" into _risk_reconcile_missing_positions. (5) The C1 guard `if position_error:` (event_demo_exits.py:1401) is False, so the loop runs and orphan-closes EVERY open trade with require_evidence=False (1418-1419). _orphan_close_pnl_backfill returning {} does NOT block the close on this path — _orphan_close_trade_row only returns None when require_evidence is True (1441). This exact behavior is locked in by the PASSING test test_risk_reconciler_closes_orphan_when_position_missing (test_liquidity_migration_event_demo_exits.py:1309-1325): position_by_symbol={}, position_error="" → kept.is_empty(), one close row. The existing protection (test_transient_get_positions_failure... line 3350; FakePrivateClient.get_positions RAISES when fail_positions=True, line 124-127) only covers the raised-exception case, never the retCode=0-empty-list case. The ws_state_cache guard (ws_state_cache.py:172-180) is identical in shape: it only refuses to overwrite when position_error is non-empty (line 177), so an empty list with empty error overwrites the cache to flat. The prior CRITICAL orphan-close fix's own documented third part — 'add consecutive-empty guard before bulk orphan-close' (memory audit-2026-05-29) — was never implemented; grep finds no consecutive/empty-count/distrust guard anywhere. Trigger realism: the wrong-settleCoin and >200-position scenarios are not realistic for this 3-sleeve USDT account, but a transient Bybit backend returning retCode=0 with an empty/partial page IS a real soft-failure mode, and it is completely unguarded. Severity high not critical: demo-only today (account often flat → no open trades to wipe, and the cycle path uses require_evidence=True so it is already safe), narrow trigger, reduce-only caps each close at position size; but on the shared reconcile authority it corrupts the ledger across all 3 sleeves with zero/fabricated-PnL closes and would dump every position at market if REAL_MONEY is ever toggled (the memory note flags this exact class as 'unbounded loss if REAL_MONEY ever enabled').
verdict.fix_notes: Direction is correct and side-effect-light. Preferred minimal implementation: in _risk_reconcile_missing_positions, when position_by_symbol is empty AND open_trades is non-empty AND position_error=="", force require_evidence=True semantics for that pass (the parameter and the fail-closed machinery already exist — reuse them rather than adding a new code path). This does NOT deadlock a legitimately-flat account: a genuine simultaneous flat-out leaves real closed-PnL records, so _orphan_close_pnl_backfill returns evidence and each trade still closes (just via the evidence path); a spurious empty read leaves trades OPEN with the existing warning until evidence appears — the desired fail-closed behavior. Avoid the auditor's literal 'detect freshly-fetched REST vs WS-maintained map' wording: reconcile_positions cannot cleanly tell which source produced self.state.positions_by_symbol (rest_reconcile UNIONs prefetch with the WS map at line 1327, on_position_message mutates it in place), so a source-discrimination guard is fragile. An even more robust variant matching the prior fix's documented intent is a consecutive-empty counter on PrivateStateCache/ws_risk (require N consecutive empty REST reads before allowing bulk orphan-close), but the single-pass require_evidence escalation is the smaller, lower-risk change. Either way add a regression test mirroring test_risk_reconciler_closes_orphan_when_position_missing but asserting that empty-map + empty-error + non-empty open_trades keeps trades OPEN (no mass close). Note the fix must cover BOTH the ws_risk _risk_reconcile_missing_positions path AND the ws_state_cache.seed/replace_with_rest_snapshot overwrite (ws_state_cache.py:177) — otherwise the cache still launders the empty fetch into a flat snapshot that the cycle's own reconcile consumes; guarding only one layer leaves the other exposed.

title: Residual-momentum SELECTION gate reads a strictly-FUTURE residual (look-ahead) because the engine's day+1 stamp offset eats the .shift(1)
evidence: The engine feature grid stamps a daily-close signal at ts_ms = day_start_ms + MS_PER_DAY (00:00 of D+1) — see volume_features and _daily_return_frame:568. The rmom table is built off build_factor_panel -> build_feature_panel -> _aggregate_daily_klines, whose ts_ms is the START-OF-DAY grid (00:00 of D, no +MS_PER_DAY). residual_return[grid=G] is the residual of fwd_ret_1d, and _attach_forward_returns uses entry=first-bar close of G+1, exit=first-bar close of G+2 — i.e. residual_return[grid=G] is realized over the window (G+1 -> G+2), strictly FORWARD of EOD-G. _attach_residual_momentum joins on _rm_day = floor(ts_ms to day): the engine signal for trading-day D (ts_ms=(D+1)00:00) matches the rmom row with grid ts_ms=(D+1)00:00, whose value is residual_momentum[grid=D+1] = rolling_sum(7).shift(1) = sum residual_return[grid (D-6)..D]. The newest term residual_return[grid=D] covers the (D+1 -> D+2) window, which is realized AFTER the EOD-D decision (the trade enters at (D+1)+1h). The shift(1) intended to drop the signal day, but the 1-day stamp-vs-grid offset consumes it, so exactly one future residual leaks into the gate. This is exactly the documented-but-UNCLEARED debt #4 in docs/research_summary.md:726-728.
impact: The age300+rmom stack is the open research lead and the rmom gate is LIVE on the continuous demo sleeve. A look-ahead term means the gate's measured all-weather lift (and the continuous sleeve's signal) is partially fitted on information unavailable at decision time -> the alpha is overstated and may not survive a causal re-run. Forward-demo would eventually expose it, but in-sample MAR/IC cited for promotion is contaminated.
proposed_fix: Make the rmom table's ts_ms convention identical to the engine's signal stamp (shift the table to day+1) OR change the join so residual_momentum[D] sums residual_return[grid D-7 .. D-1] where residual_return[grid g] is realized over (g+1->g+2) and g+2 <= EOD-D. Concretely, the newest residual term must end no later than the signal close: require the last summed grid day g satisfy g+2 <= D+1, i.e. g <= D-1 in stamp space (one more day of lag than the current shift(1)). Add a direct causality test (build the table with end=D, confirm residual_momentum[D] is byte-identical to a build with end=D+10) and a unit test asserting the newest contributing residual window ends <= signal close.

verdict.reasoning:
Traced the full causal chain on real code; the look-ahead is real on BOTH the engine backtest gate and the LIVE continuous sleeve.

(1) Engine signal-stamp: volume_features._daily_bars (volume_features.py:104) and _daily_return_frame (volume_events_features.py:568) both stamp ts_ms = day_start_ms + MS_PER_DAY, so the signal for trading-day D is stamped at (D+1) 00:00 (decision = EOD-D).

(2) rmom-table grid: precompute -> build_factor_panel -> build_feature_panel -> _aggregate_daily_klines (signal_harness.py:169) stamps ts_ms = day_start_ms with NO +MS_PER_DAY. So the same calendar day uses two different ts conventions.

(3) Forward-return window: _attach_forward_returns (signal_harness.py:730-732) sets entry = first_bar_close(g+1), exit = first_bar_close(g+2); the explicit causality-contract test (test_liquidity_migration_signal_harness.py:138, fwd_ret_1d for D0 = closes[48]/closes[24]) confirms residual_return[grid=g] covers window (g+1 -> g+2), realized at ~(g+2) 01:00.

(4) rmom = residual_return.rolling_sum(7, min_samples=4).shift(1) (precompute:112) — a single shift(1).

(5) Engine join (_attach_residual_momentum:340-341, floor-to-day, no offset): signal at (D+1)00:00 -> rmom row at (D+1)00:00 -> residual_momentum = sum residual_return[grid (D-6)..D]; newest term grid g=D covers (D+1 -> D+2), which is entirely AFTER the EOD-D decision (D+1)00:00 and even after the (D+1)01:00 entry. Exactly one future residual leaks. The shift(1) was meant to drop the signal day but the day-stamp-vs-grid +1 offset consumes it.

(6) Continuous LIVE sleeve (cross_sectional_decile:220-221, day_ts = floor(ts_ms); called from continuous_demo.py:426 in the live cycle; gate active via continuous_profile rmom_quantile=0.33): a same-day-D hourly signal (ts_ms in D 00:00..23:00) -> day_ts = D 00:00 -> residual_momentum = sum residual_return[grid (D-7)..(D-1)]; newest term grid g=D-1 covers (D -> D+1), realized at (D+1)01:00 — strictly after EVERY day-D signal hour. So the live continuous decile selection reads a strictly-future residual too. STATE confirms the live signal is bit-identical to the backtest, so the leak contaminates the in-sample continuous MAR/IC AND the live sleeve's symbol selection.

This is exactly documented debt #4 in docs/research_summary.md (HIGH, UNCONFIRMED) — the auditor's analysis resolves it as CONFIRMED. No compensating offset, no causality test exists. Severity high (not critical): it overstates a research-stage gate's measured lift and biases an in-sample promotion metric, but it is a methodology/alpha-faking surface on a demo-only sleeve, not a fund-losing live-execution bug.
verdict.fix_notes:
The fix DIRECTION (add lag so the newest summed residual is fully realized at decision time) is correct, but the proposed MAGNITUDE and one of the two options are wrong/unsafe:

1) shift amount is INSUFFICIENT. The auditor prescribes "one more day of lag than shift(1)" (= shift(2)) and states the boundary as g+2 <= D+1. But because the forward return is entry@first-bar(g+1) / exit@first-bar(g+2), residual_return[g] only completes at ~(g+2) 01:00, NOT at the close of g+1. For the engine (decision = (D+1)00:00) strict causality needs (g+2) 01:00 <= (D+1) 00:00 => g+2 <= D => g <= D-2. With rolling_sum(7).shift(s) the engine join's newest grid term is g = (D+1) - s, so we need s >= 3, i.e. shift(3) (two more than the current shift(1)), not shift(2). shift(2) still leaks the residual_return[g=D-1] window (D -> D+1) which realizes at (D+1)01:00, after the (D+1)00:00 decision. The continuous sleeve (day_ts = floor(ts_ms), earliest signal D 00:00) likewise needs g <= D-3 => s >= 3. So shift(3) is the minimal causal lag for BOTH paths under this codebase's entry@+1/exit@+2 convention.

2) The alternative "shift the table to day+1" is NOT side-effect-free. The two consumers join with DIFFERENT conventions: the engine joins on a +1-offset stamp ((D+1)00:00), the continuous sleeve joins on day_ts = floor(actual hourly ts_ms) (no offset). Re-stamping the shared residual_momentum.parquet by +1 day fixes the engine alignment but shifts the continuous join by a day (and would also need the precompute pad/live-staleness logic re-derived), breaking the live<->backtest bit-identity STATE relies on. Any fix must be applied as additional lag in the SUM (shift), not as a stamp re-mapping, OR adjusted per-consumer.

3) Both consumers share one parquet + shared join logic, so increasing the shift changes BOTH the engine backtest gate and the LIVE continuous sleeve simultaneously — by design this is what's wanted, but it means a re-run of the cited age300+rmom and continuous in-sample MAR/IC numbers is required after the fix (the measured lift will likely shrink).

4) The auditor's two proposed tests are good and should be kept: (a) build-with-end=D byte-identical to build-with-end=D+10 for residual_momentum[<=D] (append-only/causality), and (b) a unit test asserting the newest contributing residual window ends <= signal close — but (b) must encode the entry-delay (exit at first-bar of g+2 ~01:00), or it will green-light the insufficient shift(2).

title: Binance funding undercount: hardcoded funding_interval_min=480 collapses real 4h settlements into 8h buckets, dropping ~half the funding cost
evidence: _normalize_binance_funding hardcodes funding_interval_min = 8*60 for EVERY Binance symbol (line 749), unlike _normalize_funding (Bybit) which reads the per-symbol fundingIntervalHour (line 798). Binance settles some alts every 4h, but the raw rows already arrive at the true settlement cadence (one row per fundingTime). _funding_lookup then buckets by ts_ms // (interval_min*60_000) and keeps .first() per bucket (lines 437-439): with interval=480 (8h) but actual 4h spacing, two consecutive real 4h settlements fall in the same 8h bucket and the second is DROPPED. For a short paying positive funding this removes a real cost -> inflates net_return. Documented as the single most important open debt (#1, research_summary.md:715-720).
impact: Binance is the cross-venue OOS arbiter and funding eats ~85% of the intraday edge; understating Binance funding ~50% on 4h-funding alts INFLATES the Binance MAR the Tier-2/Tier-3 promotion gate trusts. Directly fakes the cross-venue alpha used for promotion decisions.
proposed_fix: Either fetch the true per-symbol funding interval from Binance (fundingInfo / premiumIndex endpoints expose fundingIntervalHours) and store it, or DON'T collapse Binance rows at all (the raw rows are already one-per-settlement, so the 8h-snapshot-dedup logic that Bybit needs is inapplicable to Binance — gate the collapse on a per-symbol real interval, defaulting to 'no collapse' when interval is unknown). Re-run the Binance promotion-gate MAR after the fix.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED with quantitative evidence on the actual promotion-gate data root. Mechanism traced end-to-end and verified against on-disk data:

1. CODE: `_normalize_binance_funding` (downloaders.py:749) hardcodes `funding_interval_min = 8*60 = 480` for EVERY Binance symbol — unlike Bybit's `_normalize_funding` (downloaders.py:798) which reads per-symbol `fundingIntervalHour`. The raw rows come from `/fapi/v1/fundingRate` (binance.py:54-63), which returns exactly one row per real settlement (`fundingTime`).

2. COLLAPSE: `_funding_lookup` (trade_lifecycle.py:428-441) buckets `ts_ms // (funding_interval_min*60_000)` and keeps `.first()` per bucket. With interval=480 (8h) but real 4h spacing, two consecutive 4h settlements land in the same 8h bucket and the second is DROPPED. The collapsed rate list feeds `_perp_funding_return` (trade_lifecycle.py:482-488) → `funding_return` → `net_return` (volume_events.py:1491-1502). For a short book this drops a real per-settlement funding cost/credit, distorting net_return.

3. DATA (decisive): On `~/SHARED_DATA/binance_full_pit_strategy/funding` — the root `verify_div_promotion.py` uses as the Binance promotion-gate venue, read by `volume_events`/`long_native` via `read_dataset(root,"funding")` — ALL 10,719 sampled rows carry `funding_interval_min=480`, yet the DOMINANT real settlement cadence is 4.0h (7,040 gaps vs 1,532 at 8h; 908 at 1h; 40 distinct symbols settle at 4h). Replaying the exact collapse on the full funding dataset (129,134 rows): 53,475 rows (41.4%) are DROPPED, and 44.7% of total funding-rate magnitude is discarded. This matches the auditor's ~50% undercount claim almost exactly.

4. Counter-claim rebutted: research_summary's "Binance funding genuinely ≈0" refers to the MEAN SIGNED rate (−6e-6, near zero only because longs/shorts cancel cross-sectionally). Funding on a short is booked per-settlement and is path-dependent; dropping ~45% of the per-settlement magnitude is a real cost-model error, not a no-op. The "missing"-funding language elsewhere in research_summary applies to the OTHER Binance root (`binance_full_pit`, which has only `binance_usdm_funding/` and no `funding/` dir, so `read_dataset(root,"funding")` returns empty there) — but the strategy root DOES carry and consume funding, so the bug is live on the daily-short and long sleeves, and on the continuous sleeve via `_autodetect_dataset_names` → `binance_usdm_funding`.

Severity HIGH (not critical): Binance is the cross-venue OOS arbiter and this understates its funding cost on the ~45% of settlements that are sub-8h, inflating the Binance MAR the Tier-2/Tier-3 gate trusts — directly biasing a promotion-decision metric. Not critical because it does not corrupt the live trading/order path (live funding is exchange-settled, not modeled) and nothing is promoted to real money; it biases a research/gate number, which is exactly the data-integrity class.
verdict.fix_notes:
The proposed fix is correct in direction and side-effect-safe IF implemented as a value-correction at normalization time rather than a blanket disable of the collapse. Specifics and caveats:

WHY the collapse must NOT be globally removed: `_funding_lookup`'s collapse exists for the Bybit case where `get_funding_history` can return intra-interval SNAPSHOT rows (multiple rows for one real 8h settlement). Deleting the collapse for everyone would re-introduce up-to-8x funding over-billing on Bybit. So the fix must be Binance-scoped (or interval-driven), not a blanket removal.

PREFERRED FIX (also fixes a latent Bybit issue I found): the root cause is the WRONG `funding_interval_min` being stamped, not the collapse algorithm. For Binance, `/fapi/v1/fundingRate` returns one row per settlement with no intra-interval snapshots, so the safest minimal fix is to compute the true per-symbol interval from the data itself: in `_normalize_binance_funding`, derive `funding_interval_min` from the modal consecutive `fundingTime` gap per symbol (or fetch `fundingIntervalHours` from `/fapi/v1/fundingInfo` and store it). With the real interval stamped, the existing collapse becomes a no-op for Binance (each settlement already sits in its own bucket) and remains correct for any future snapshot rows. Defaulting to "no collapse" (e.g. interval = min observed gap, or a sentinel that makes each row its own bucket) when the interval is unknown is acceptable for Binance specifically.

CAVEAT the auditor missed: I also observed the BYBIT strategy/full_pit funding data carries `funding_interval_min=480` uniformly despite real 4h/1h/2h gaps — i.e. `_normalize_funding`'s `row.get("fundingIntervalHour", 8)` was apparently defaulting to 8 (field absent/unpopulated at download time). So the same undercount may exist on Bybit, not just Binance. The fix should therefore stamp the true per-symbol interval on BOTH venues (and re-download or re-derive the stored `funding_interval_min`), not only patch the Binance normalizer — otherwise the Bybit baseline that the cross-venue comparison rests on stays biased.

VALIDATION required (must be a fresh pre-registered run): after the fix, re-run the Binance (and Bybit) promotion-gate MAR via the r1_robustness / volume_events_cell path on the corrected roots and compare. title: Live failed-fade (ff6) bars_held counts from the actual fill cycle-time, not the engine's entry_ready bar — ff6 timing can differ from the backtest by a bar near the 6h boundary

The existing ff6 test (test_liquidity_migration_event_demo_planning.py:435-494) only exercises entry_ts_ms == entry-bar-open (no lag), so it never catches this. The promoted-profile comment "live _failed_fade_exit_since_entry is logic-identical to the backtest" (event_demo.py:1561) is therefore overstated for late fills. Severity medium, not higher: this is a demo/paper forward-research system (no real money), the offset is bounded by max_entry_lag, ff6 is a loss-mitigation exit whose worst case is firing somewhat later toward the hard stop, and it affects exit-attribution / live reproduction of the ff6-MAR claim rather than causing capital loss or wrong fills.

title: Continuous live sleeve caps entry qty at maxOrderQty instead of splitting — silently under-sizes large entries vs backtest
evidence: `_execute_continuous_entries` calls `order_quantity_for_notional(..., max_order_qty=max_qty)` (line 830), which floors the qty to the venue per-order cap (event_demo.py:1514-1516) and never splits. impact: On a low-priced, high-qty continuous candidate whose target exceeds Bybit's per-order cap, the live position is silently smaller than the backtest assumed — biasing the continuous forward-demo (the sleeve's only OOS arbiter) toward under-exposure and breaking the live==backtest fidelity the sleeve is being validated on. proposed_fix: Mirror the short sleeve: pass max_order_qty=0.0 to order_quantity_for_notional and split the entry via _split_qty_for_max_order_size, persisting max_market_order_qty on the trade (already done at line 896) so the exit split matches.

The short sleeve deliberately passes `max_order_qty=0.0` and splits via `_split_qty_for_max_order_size` (event_demo_entries.py:212-243) specifically to stop the observed cap-and-reduce under-sizing (REQUSDT at 53% of target). `contract.max_market_order_qty` is populated from Bybit's `maxMktOrderQty` (downloaders.py:866), so `max_qty` is a real binding value, and the sleeve is LIVE with SUBMIT_ORDERS=1 (STATE.md:33). So on a cheap coin whose target qty exceeds maxMktOrderQty, the live continuous position is silently smaller than the backtest assumed — a genuine live-vs-backtest fidelity divergence on the sleeve's own forward-demo arbiter.

Severity stays LOW (not higher): the continuous sleeve sizes at only ~2% equity per name (~$200 on the $10k fallback equity), vs the much larger short sleeve where the binding was originally observed. For a ~$200 market order to exceed maxMktOrderQty requires a very cheap, low-market-cap perp (e.g. ~$0.001 price with a ~100k market cap). Possible and concrete, but rare and bounded; the auditor's own impact note concedes this. Not a correctness/safety bug (the position is internally consistent today — held qty == capped qty <= cap, so the exit closes cleanly), purely a research-fidelity bias.
verdict.fix_notes:
The fix DIAGNOSIS is right (mirror the short sleeve: pass max_order_qty=0.0 + split the entry) but it is INCOMPLETE and as-written introduces a new bug. The fix claims the exit is already handled because max_market_order_qty is persisted (line 896) "so the exit split matches." That is only half-true. There are TWO continuous exit paths:
 (1) the PRIMARY in-cycle exit `_execute_continuous_exits` (continuous_demo.py:752-754) submits a SINGLE reduce-only market order of the full stored `qty` and does NOT split and does NOT read max_market_order_qty;
 (2) ws_risk.ws_exit (ws_risk.py:1149-1157) DOES split — but that is the orphan-close/reconcile fallback, not the normal cycle exit.
Today path (1) is safe only because the entry CAPS the held qty (<= maxMktOrderQty). If you split the entry (holding the full uncapped qty) WITHOUT also splitting `_execute_continuous_exits`, then on exactly the cheap-coin trades this fix targets, the normal left_decile/breakeven/failed_fade/max_hold exit becomes a single reduce-only order > maxMktOrderQty -> Bybit rejects it (status="failed", line 757) and the position fails to close via its primary path. That is strictly worse than the current under-sizing.

title: Symbol-only orphan-close keying ignores the side-aware helper that exists for exactly the flip case
evidence: `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions` decides a trade is an orphan by `symbol in position_by_symbol` (symbol-only). The codebase ships `_position_size_by_symbol_side` (event_demo.py:2449-2477) whose docstring explicitly warns that symbol-only keying lets a short→long same-symbol flip hide a stale short ('Keying only by symbol would let the orphan reconciler keep the stale short trade as still open'), yet the active reconciler does not use it. Today this is masked because each sleeve filters entries against the full-account `live_position_symbols`, so two sleeves cannot both hold the same symbol — but that cross-sleeve exclusion is the ONLY thing preventing the flip, and a manual venue-side flip on the shared account would not be caught.
impact: Latent ledger drift: a same-symbol side flip (manual close+reopen on the shared account, or any future relaxation of the account-wide exclusion) leaves a stale ledger trade marked open with no matching position, so its stop/exit logic keeps running against a position that no longer exists on that side.
proposed_fix: Key the orphan check on (symbol, side) using the already-present `_position_size_by_symbol_side` so a flip is correctly surfaced as a short-side orphan close while leaving the new long untouched.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed asymmetry. Two orphan-reconcile paths exist: the cycle path `_reconcile_open_trades` (event_demo_exits.py:1357) was explicitly fixed to key by `(symbol, trade_side)` via `_position_size_by_symbol_side` and has a flip-case test (`test_reconcile_open_trades_closes_when_position_flipped_to_opposite_side`, tests/test_liquidity_migration_event_demo_exits.py:1261). The ws_risk path `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions` (event_demo_exits.py:1407) still uses symbol-only `symbol in position_by_symbol` and has NO flip-case test. Per the project's architecture memory, ws_risk is the SINGLE live reconcile authority on the netted shared account, so the symbol-only path is the one running live.

Reachability traced: on a WS position message (ws_risk.py:649-664), a short->long flip stores the new long row at `positions_by_symbol[symbol]` (line 657), then `reconcile_positions` -> `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions` sees `symbol in position_by_symbol` True and KEEPS the stale short trade open (event_demo_exits.py:1407-1409). Its stop/exit logic then runs against a short that no longer exists on that side. Same via the REST snapshot path (`_active_position_by_symbol`, event_demo.py:2239, single-key-per-symbol). The cycle-path `(symbol, side)` check at line 1357 would correctly orphan-close it.

Why LOW, not higher: the bug is genuinely latent. The engine itself can never create a same-symbol flip because every sleeve (short event_demo.py:442, long long_native_event_demo.py:533, continuous continuous_demo.py:1085) filters entry candidates against the account-wide `live_position_symbols`, so two sleeves never hold the same symbol. Triggering requires an external/manual venue-side flip (close+reopen opposite side) on the shared account, or a future relaxation of the cross-sleeve exclusion. The auditor's framing (masked by the account-wide exclusion; that exclusion is the only thing preventing it) is accurate. Impact is ledger drift on one trade, not real-money loss (demo/paper account), and not a methodology/look-ahead correctness bug. low/data-integrity is correct.

It only NARROWS the keep-open branch, so no new false orphan-closes; the existing position_error guard (line 1401-1402) still prevents the transient-empty-read wipe. Confirmed side-effect-free.\n\nBUT the literal proposed mechanism ('use _position_size_by_symbol_side') is NOT a clean drop-in for this path: that helper takes a list[dict] of raw positions, whereas `_risk_reconcile_missing_positions` and its two callers (ws_risk.py:1280 and event_demo.py:1168) pass a symbol-keyed `position_by_symbol: dict[str, dict]`. The position records stored in that dict DO carry a `side` field (via `_active_position_by_symbol` / WS row at ws_risk.py:657), so the minimal correct fix is to keep the symbol-keyed signature and compare the trade's normalized side against the position's normalized side, e.g. replace lines 1407-1409 with: `pos = position_by_symbol.get(symbol); if symbol and pos is not None and _normalized_position_side(pos.get('side')) == _normalized_position_side(trade.get('side')): kept.append(trade); continue`. (Import `_normalized_position_side` into event_demo_exits.py if not already present.) Add a ws_risk-path flip-case test mirroring the existing cycle-path test. Avoid changing the function signature to a list unless both callers are updated to retain raw_positions, which they currently do not at reconcile time.

title: WS fill-confirmation returns on the FIRST fill row, can record a multi-fill market order as partial
evidence: `_wait_for_execution_summary` returns immediately once the execution router has ANY fill row with qty>0 (`if _float(summary.get('qty')) > 0.0: return summary`). For a market order that fills in multiple executions, the WS stream may deliver the first partial before the rest; the function returns the partial-sum, the caller computes filled_qty < target and stamps status 'partial'/'submitted_unconfirmed' and a too-small filled_notional, even though the order completed microseconds later. The next reconcile/residual-pickup corrects it, so it is self-healing, not a money error.
impact: Transient under-reported entry/exit fill in the ledger on multi-fill market orders, corrected on the next reconcile cycle. No position drift (reduce-only/residual pickup handles it) but it adds noise to fill-time/notional fidelity used by the paper<->demo reconciliation.
proposed_fix: When returning a WS-sourced summary whose qty is below the order target, keep polling (REST or WS) until the order is terminal or the deadline, rather than returning on the first partial — or gate the early-return on the order being reported terminal (orderStatus Filled) rather than qty>0.

verdict.reasoning: Traced a concrete triggering path. Deployed entry order type is "Market" (event_demo.py:70 default `entry_order_type="Market"`), and market orders routinely fill across multiple book levels as separate executions. The private WS execution stream delivers each execution as a separate message — confirmed by test_router_accumulates_partial_fills_in_order (two on_execution_event calls → two rows). ExecutionEventRouter.wait_for_fill_rows wakes as soon as the link has ANY buffered row (execution_router.py:106 `while not self._rows.get(order_link_id)`) and returns a snapshot of whatever has accumulated; the immediate-return test confirms it does not wait for more. _wait_for_execution_summary (event_demo.py:2436-2439) then returns on the first `_float(summary.get("qty")) > 0.0`, so if the wait wakes after the first execution message but before later ones, it returns the partial sum. The caller (event_demo_entries.py:488-498) computes sub_filled_qty < sub_target → sub_status="partial" and an under-sized sub_notional/filled_notional (lines 507, 554), and the order row is written status="partial". Self-healing is genuine and idempotent: "partial" is in PENDING_ORDER_STATUSES (_common.py:26), so the next cycle's _reconcile_pending_order_fills (event_demo_exits.py:428-642) re-reads via REST get_trade_history (gets the COMPLETE cumulative venue fill), computes delta_qty = filled_qty - previous_filled_qty, and delta-adds it onto the open trade — correcting qty, weighted entry_price, notional_usdt, and initial_margin_usdt (lines 611-642), with previous_filled_qty written back each pass for idempotency. So no position drift and no money error; the only impact is a transient under-reported fill_qty/notional/fill-time in the ledger that adds noise to the paper<->demo reconciliation until the next cycle corrects it. Severity low, exactly as the auditor characterized. Note the early-return-on-any-positive-qty pattern is NOT WS-exclusive: the REST branch at event_demo.py:2441 also returns on the first `qty > 0.0` regardless of target, so a mid-fill REST snapshot can under-report the same way.
verdict.fix_notes: The target-qty variant of the proposed fix is correct and side-effect-free; the "gate on orderStatus==Filled" variant is fragile and should NOT be used. Concretely: thread the sub-order target qty into _wait_for_execution_summary and only early-return when summary_qty + tolerance >= target_qty; otherwise keep looping (WS then REST) until target-met OR `time.monotonic() >= deadline`. The deadline backstop at event_demo.py:2441 already bounds the loop, so a market order that genuinely under-fills (rare) still returns its partial at the deadline — and the at-deadline REST get_trade_history call (line 2440) captures the cumulative fill, which is strictly more complete than the WS partial. This strictly improves fidelity with no correctness downside and no infinite-loop risk. Two caveats the auditor's framing understates: (1) the fix must cover BOTH early-returns — the WS branch (line 2438) AND the REST branch (line 2441) — not just WS, or a mid-fill REST snapshot reintroduces the same under-report; (2) avoid gating on orderStatus=="Filled": the router stores raw execution rows and the code never reads cumExecQty/orderStatus from them (the only orderStatus read is at line 2085 in an unrelated order-history path), so that field is not reliably present in the WS execution rows and gating on it would either no-op the early-return (always falling through to the 2.0s deadline → latency regression) or behave inconsistently across schema versions. The target-qty comparison is robust because the caller already knows the exact sub_target. Minor expected cost: for any order that does not fully fill within the WS fast window (e.g., a Limit entry if entry_order_type is reconfigured), the function now blocks up to order_fill_confirm_seconds (default 2.0s) per sub-order instead of returning early; this is bounded, parallelized across the entry ThreadPoolExecutor, and not a correctness issue.

title: Paper/demo cycle books stop-loss and take-profit exits at the trigger price (optimistic 'stop' fill), diverging from the deployed bar_extreme_capped engine — paper arbiter over-states alpha
lines: event_demo_planning.py:272-285 (stop) & 287-304 (tp), event_demo_exits.py:322-333 (exit_price=planned_exit_price when no venue fill)
evidence: `plan_demo_exits` returns `planned_price = stop_price` for a stop hit and `take_profit_price` for a TP hit (the TRIGGER price). In `_execute_exits` the dry-run/paper branch (`not demo.submit_orders`) sets `fully_filled=True` and `exit_price = planned_exit_price`, then books `gross_trade_return = _trade_return(entry, stop_price)`. The deployed backtest engine default is `bar_extreme_capped` (STATE.md 'Engine defaults'), which fills a stop at min(stop, low)/max(stop, high) capped at 10% — strictly worse than the trigger for a gap-through bar. So the PAPER sleeve (the forward arbiter, per the three-tier gate) systematically books stop exits BETTER than both the backtest and the real demo (which fills at the venue's actual price via closed_pnl backfill). Reconciliation will read this as paper out-performing backtest on every stop/TP exit.
impact: The paper-shadow ledger — explicitly the OOS arbiter for promotion (Tier-2/Tier-3) — overstates returns on every stop and TP exit by the trigger-vs-realized-fill gap. Inflates the metric that gates real-money promotion. Backtesting-error #3 (instantaneous trading at the observed price) / #14 (impossible OHLC fill).
proposed_fix: In the paper (non-submit) exit path, apply the same `_stop_fill_price(mode=bar_extreme_capped)` slippage model the engine uses when the exit_reason is stop_loss/take_profit, using the triggering bar's high/low rather than the bare trigger price. Reuse volume_events._stop_fill_price so paper, backtest, and demo agree.

verdict.reasoning:
The STOP half of the mechanism is real and traces to a concrete live path with the deployed `promoted` profile (stop_loss_pct=0.12 is enabled, not overridden). In `plan_demo_exits` (event_demo_planning.py:272-285), an intrabar stop found via `_stop_hit_since_entry` (event_demo.py:2600 — detects on bar `high>=stop` for a short) is booked with `planned_price = stop_price` (bare trigger, line 283). In `_execute_exits` paper mode (`not demo.submit_orders`, event_demo_exits.py:323-333) `exit_price = planned_exit_price` and `gross_trade_return = _trade_return(entry, stop_price)`. The deployed backtest fills stops at `bar_extreme_capped` (volume_events.py:1409,1568-1582) — strictly worse than the trigger on a gap-through bar. So the paper ledger's stop exits are systematically better than the backtest's. The `-paper.service` (SUBMIT_ORDERS=0, RECORD_DRY_RUN=1) is live, and STATE.md Tier-3 references the forward demo/paper ledgers as the OOS arbiter, so the path is reachable and relevant.

BUT the finding is substantially overstated and is low severity, for three reasons:
1. The TP half is FALSE. The backtest fills take-profit at the bare `take_profit_price` trigger (volume_events.py:1417 — no slippage, no cap), identical to what paper books. There is NO paper-vs-backtest divergence on TP. The claim of "every stop/TP exit" is wrong on TP.
2. The paper sleeve is BY DESIGN an idealized-fill baseline, not a realistic-execution model. reconciliation.py's own docstring (lines 1-7): "The paper runner records idealized fills at the signal price; the demo runner records actual Bybit demo fills... measures execution slippage." Paper entries are also idealized (event_demo_entries.py:553 books `entry_price=price`). The demo sleeve (SUBMIT_ORDERS=1) books REAL venue fills via closed_pnl and is the honest execution ledger; the Tier-3 MAR is anchored on the demo real-fill ledger plus the bar_extreme_capped backtest, not on the paper ledger's absolute return. So "inflates the metric that gates real-money promotion" overstates the impact — the demo ledger and backtest both fill stops realistically.
3. The genuinely valid residual: paper's stop fill (bare trigger) is even better than the backtest's idealized-capped fill, so the backtest↔paper reconcile carries a small systematic paper-beats-backtest gap on the stop-exit subset only. That is a minor consistency defect in the shadow, and the reconcile is explicitly there to surface/quantify exactly this slippage. It is not a hidden look-ahead or a silent inflation of the gate.

Net: real mechanism on stops, but mislabeled (TP claim false), wrong about which ledger gates promotion, and the divergence is the documented idealized-baseline behavior that reconciliation is designed to measure. Not high; low.
verdict.fix_notes: The proposed fix is partially incorrect and not a clean drop-in. (1) It says apply bar_extreme_capped when exit_reason is stop_loss OR take_profit — applying it to take_profit is WRONG: the backtest fills TP at the bare trigger (volume_events.py:1417), so capping TP would CREATE a new paper-worse-than-backtest divergence in the opposite direction. Only the stop_loss path should change. title: Same-hour cover-then-re-entry produces a duplicate trade_id (and duplicate Bybit orderLinkId): the closed trade is silently dropped from the ledger / the re-entry order is rejected

proposed_fix: Make the ledger key collision-proof: build trade_id from a monotonic open instant (entry_ts_ms / now_ms) rather than the shared signal_ts (keep signal_ts as a separate column), OR add a per-open sequence suffix; and add a per-account-unique nonce/sequence to the entry orderLinkId so a same-hour re-entry cannot reuse a prior link. verdict.reasoning:
Traced and confirmed the full code path on deployed sleeves.

Same-cycle re-entry is blocked (the just-closed exit_ts_ms is inside the cooldown), so the collision requires a LATER cycle in the same hour -- and the full entry cycle runs every INTERVAL_SECONDS=60 (deploy/systemd/liquidity-migration-bybit-continuous-demo.service), ~60 cycles/hour, so cross-cycle same-hour re-entry is routine.

So the newer OPEN re-entry row wins and the CLOSED row (with realized PnL / exit_ts / net_return) is permanently dropped from the parquet. This is the live behavior of the PAPER sleeve (SUBMIT_ORDERS=0, RECORD_DRY_RUN=1, PAPER_MODE=1), where the entry trade row is always written (line 883 guard "not demo.submit_orders" is True) -- a realized fade vanishes, breaking accounting/reconcile and understating trade count.

Consequence 2 (lost signal): on the LIVE demo sleeve (SUBMIT_ORDERS=1), the duplicate entry orderLinkId is rejected by Bybit; place_order raises, caught at lines 863-864 -> submit_mode="error", filled_qty=0 -> the line-883 guard fails -> no trade row written -> the valid D9 re-entry is silently missed.

verdict.fix_notes:
The bug is real, but the proposed fix as written is NOT side-effect-free, because trade_id is contractually coupled to the orderLinkId.

ws_risk's rebuild-safe recovery (ws_risk.py:1461-1472, _build_adopted_trade) reconstructs trade_id = f"{strategy_id}-{symbol}-{signal_ts_ms}" by decoding the Bybit-retained orderLinkId back to signal_ts via decode_entry_order_link_id (order_link_id.py:51-89, which returns only (sleeve, signal_ts_ms)). The deterministic trade_id MUST stay derivable from (strategy_id, symbol, decode(orderLinkId)). 

The proposed half "build trade_id from entry_ts_ms/now_ms instead of signal_ts" therefore BREAKS that reconstruction: after a VPS rebuild the local ledger is gone, ws_risk re-derives trade_id from the orderLinkId, and an entry-instant-based trade_id is not encoded anywhere in the orderLinkId -> the recovered trade_id no longer matches the original -> the position falls back to the lossy adopted-* path, reintroducing the very orphan-mismatch class this code exists to prevent (and not just for continuous -- the reconstruction path is shared by short/long too).

A simpler alternative that avoids the encoding contract entirely: extend the re-entry suppression to cover the full signal_ts period (i.e., block re-opening a symbol whose last entry shares the current signal_ts, or set the effective cooldown >= 60 min / >= the signal_ts granularity) so a collision can never form in the first place. The auditor's requested regression test (cover-then-re-enter within the same deciding-bar hour -> two distinct trade_ids AND orderLinkIds, closed row survives a write/read round-trip) is the right gate, but it must also assert the VPS-rebuild reconstruction (decode orderLinkId -> trade_id) still resolves for both legs.

title: Live FC signal fires on an INCOMPLETE (partial) daily bar — look-ahead + backtest/live divergence
evidence: `_select_long_entry_candidates` builds `eligible_ts` as `sorted(ts for ts in features['ts_ms'].unique() if (now_ms - int(ts)) <= SIGNAL_FRESHNESS_MS)`. There is NO lower bound (`now_ms >= ts`). A daily bar's `ts_ms` is the day-END (next-midnight, see momentum_signals.daily_bars line 57). For the CURRENT UTC day the bar is emitted as soon as `daily_bars` sees >=20 hourly bars (`min_hourly_bars=20`), i.e. after ~20:00 UTC — verified: at 22:00 UTC `daily_bars` emits a today bar with hourly_bars=22 and close = the 21:00 hourly close (reproduced directly). That bar's `ts_ms` is FUTURE, so `now_ms - ts < 0 <= 24h` → it passes the freshness gate and is processed. FC (`detect_pattern_fomo_chase`) keys on `log_return` (today_close/yesterday_close), `close_location`, `today_volume_rank`, all computed from the PARTIAL close — exactly the intraday-pump case FC is built to catch. Dedup (lines 935-941) keeps the HIGHEST signal_ts per symbol, so the partial today-bar OVERRIDES the valid fully-closed yesterday bar. The module docstring (lines 11, 826) claims it uses 'the most-recent fully-closed UTC daily bar … yesterday if today's bar hasn't closed yet' but the code does NOT enforce closure. The short sleeve does not have this gap: it gates on a feature `ready_ts` via `max_entry_lag_minutes` (event_demo.py:67).
impact: alpha (fakes the forward-demo signal): the live long sleeve enters on intraday pumps that may reverse before the true daily close, a signal set the backtest never produces (backtest only ever sees complete 24h days) — violates backtesting-errors rules 2 (future info in signals) and 16 (same-code illusion / backtest≠live). Real demo money is committed on a price that is not the validated signal close.
proposed_fix: In `_select_long_entry_candidates`, restrict `eligible_ts` to fully-closed bars: `if ts is not None and now_ms >= int(ts) and (now_ms - int(ts)) <= SIGNAL_FRESHNESS_MS`. Equivalently drop any daily bar whose day-end ts is in the future. Add a regression test with `now_ms` set to mid-UTC-day and a partial today bar present, asserting only the closed prior-day bar is considered.

title: Paper-shadow (paper_mode/dry-run) time-stop exits record FLAT (0%) PnL — long paper ledger is unusable as a forward arbiter
evidence: `_execute_long_exits` receives NO `price_by_symbol` (compare the short sleeve, event_demo.py:299/322, which passes `_price_lookup_from_tickers_and_klines` so dry-run exits mark to live price). In the long sleeve, for the non-submit path `final_exit_price = exit_price or _float(trade.get('entry_price'))` (line 1196); in paper/dry-run `exit_price` is never set (no venue fill), so `final_exit_price == entry_price` → `gross_trade_return == 0`. Therefore EVERY paper-mode long trade is held the full 3 days and closed flat at entry price, with entry/exit fees also 0 in dry-run. The paper ledger's realized PnL is ~0 for every trade.
impact: alpha/data-integrity: the long paper shadow — an explicit B.4 slippage reference and a forward-demo arbiter input (STATE.md Tier-3) — systematically records zero realized PnL and never simulates the ATR stop/TP, so it cannot validate the sleeve or measure demo execution slippage. proposed_fix: Thread `price_by_symbol` into `_execute_long_exits` and mark dry-run/paper exits to the live ticker/kline price (mirror the short sleeve). For a faithful paper shadow also simulate the venue-managed ATR stop/TP in paper mode (e.g. close at stop/TP price when the bar path crosses it) rather than only time-stopping flat.

4. entry_price was the live signal price (line 1375 entry_price = price = price_by_symbol.get(...); persisted at line 1524). So _trade_return(entry, entry, side="long") = (entry-entry)/entry = 0.0 (event_demo.py:2844-2845), giving gross_trade_return=0 and net_return=0 for EVERY paper time-stop exit. exit_fee_usdt is also 0 in dry-run (line 1125).
5. Venue ATR stop_loss/take_profit are passed to _order_params only inside the submit_orders block (line 1405-1406), so in paper mode no protective order exists and the ONLY exit is the 3-day time-stop. Every paper long trade is therefore held the full hold window and closed flat at entry.

Asymmetry vs short sleeve is genuine: short _execute_exits (event_demo_exits.py:273-276) computes sub_avg_price = exec_summary.avg_price OR exit_plan['planned_exit_price'], and plan_demo_exits populates planned_exit_price from the live price_by_symbol — so short dry-run exits mark to live price. The long paper ledger is consumed by run_long_paper_demo_reconciliation (reconciliation.py:1355), which pairs the recorded paper trades against demo trades to measure execution slippage; it does not recompute/backfill exit prices, so the flat-zero exit PnL is exactly what is read. title: decompose_strategy_pnl day-grid off-by-one: snaps to the entry's calendar day (D+1), not the signal/decision day (D) — look-ahead exposure + 1-day-shifted factor-return window corrupts the Tier-3 residual-Sharpe gate
evidence: The factor panel (build_factor_panel -> build_feature_panel/_aggregate_daily_klines) keys ts_ms to the trading-day START = 00:00 UTC of the DECISION day D (signal_harness.py:149-169 'the bar with the smallest ts_ms on a date OPENS at 00:00'). The panel row at ts_ms=D carries factor loadings causal at D's EOD close, and factor_return[ts_ms=D] = the OLS slope of fwd_ret_1d, which _attach_forward_returns (signal_harness.py:705-740) defines as the +1h entry close of D+1 -> close of D+2 (i.e. the real tradeable return over [01:00 D+1, 01:00 D+2]). BUT the live volume_events ledger stamps signal_ts_ms = day_start + period = 00:00 of D+1 (_common.trading_day_expr docstring + volume_events.py:677,958: entry_ts_ms = signal_ts_ms + entry_delay_hours*MS_PER_HOUR = 01:00 of D+1). decompose then computes grid = (ets // MS_PER_DAY) * MS_PER_DAY = floor(01:00 D+1) = 00:00 of D+1 (one day too late). Consequence (a): exposure = load_map.get((sym, grid=D+1)) reads the D+1 loadings, which are observed at D+1's close — AFTER the trade is already open at 01:00 D+1 — i.e. look-ahead in the exposure (Error #2). Consequence (b): present_days = [D+1, D+2, ...] so the cumulative factor return sums factor_return[D+1] (period [D+2,D+3]) onward, SKIPPING factor_return[D] (the trade's actual first day [D+1,D+2]) and over-running one day past the hold. Both shift the explained component by one calendar day, so residual = realized - explained is systematically mis-booked.
impact: Fakes the alpha at the real-money gate: residual_sharpe (the Tier-3 promotion criterion, STATE.md line 116-117) is computed from a factor decomposition whose exposures are non-causal (look-ahead) and whose factor-return window is off by one day. A strategy could pass or fail Tier-3 for the wrong reason; the residual is not the true idiosyncratic alpha. Pure methodology corruption — no live-money path, but it gates the path to live money.
proposed_fix: Snap to the DECISION day, not the entry's calendar day. The trade decided on D's close enters at 00:00-01:00 of D+1, so grid should map back one day: grid = ((ets // MS_PER_DAY) - 1) * MS_PER_DAY (equivalently key on trading_day(signal_ts) = date(entry_ts - entry_delay - 1ms)). Then exposure = load_map[(sym, D)] (causal) and present_days start at factor_return[D] (the trade's real first day). Add a regression test asserting that for an entry at (D+1)*DAY+1h the resolved exposure equals the panel row at D, not D+1 (see risk-config-cli-2).

Keying on trading_day(signal_ts) via the established _common.trading_day_expr (`date(entry_ts - entry_delay - 1ms)`) is the cleaner, single-source-of-truth form and is preferred over the bare arithmetic.

BUT the proposed arithmetic `grid = ((ets // MS_PER_DAY) - 1) * MS_PER_DAY` is NOT side-effect-free as written:
1. For entry_ts_ms exactly on the grid (e.g. ets=0 in fixtures), it produces grid = -MS_PER_DAY (a negative/pre-epoch timestamp) -> unresolved.
2. It breaks at least three existing tests that hard-code the current one-day-late snapping: test_decompose_strategy_pnl_splits_explained_and_residual (entry_ts_ms=0 expects exposure at ts_ms=0), test_decompose_strategy_pnl_missing_exposure_is_null (entry_ts_ms=0), and test_decompose_strategy_pnl_snaps_offgrid_entry_to_daily_grid (expects entry at 10*DAY+1h to resolve to loadings at 10*DAY, which is the WRONG semantics the bug encodes). title: Blocking get_closed_pnl REST call runs per-orphan on the WS consumer hot path inside on_position_message — a synchronized multi-position close serially stalls stop enforcement
evidence: on_position_message → reconcile_positions(write=True) (ws_risk.py:664) passes trading_client=self.private_client (ws_risk.py:1284). _risk_reconcile_missing_positions calls _orphan_close_trade_row → _orphan_close_pnl_backfill → get_closed_pnl (event_demo_exits.py:1486), a blocking paginated REST call (bybit.py:502, follows nextPageCursor up to max_pages=50), executed on the single consumer thread for EACH orphan. During a correlated basket close (the methodology doc's 'most positions exiting in the same minute' anomaly) the WS pushes N size=0 frames; each frame's reconcile serially blocks on REST while queued ticker frames (which drive the actual stop_loss/take_profit checks in evaluate_symbols) wait behind it in self.events. The 60s daemon's stop-trigger latency degrades exactly when many positions move together.
impact: latency on the live risk hot path: delayed stop/TP enforcement during synchronized moves — the worst time to be slow; in a fast melt-up the giveback that should trigger covers is processed late.
proposed_fix: Move the closed-PnL backfill off the synchronous WS path: in on_position_message, close orphans WITHOUT a blocking REST call (mark closed with a 'pnl_backfill_pending' flag) and let rest_reconcile / the reconcile-prefetcher thread backfill exit_price/PnL asynchronously. Or batch all orphans from one frame into a single get_closed_pnl(settle_coin) sweep instead of one call per symbol.

verdict.reasoning: Traced the full path and it triggers. on_position_message (ws_risk.py:649) runs on the single consumer thread (run loop sets _consumer_thread_ident at line 491; state mutation off this thread is a hard error at 631-635). A size=0 position frame pops the symbol from positions_by_symbol (line 662), then on_position_message calls reconcile_positions(write=True) (line 664), which passes trading_client=self.private_client (line 1284), non-None and active in the live demo daemon (submit_orders=True; gate at line 1282). _risk_reconcile_missing_positions (event_demo_exits.py:1376) loops open_trades and, for each symbol now absent from position_by_symbol, calls _orphan_close_trade_row -> _orphan_close_pnl_backfill -> get_closed_pnl (event_demo_exits.py:1486) ONCE PER ORPHAN. get_closed_pnl (bybit.py:502) is a blocking, paginated REST call following nextPageCursor up to max_pages=50, routed through _call which also does rate_limiter.acquire() and a time.sleep backoff retry loop (bybit.py:694-716) — so under burst/rate-limit it can block even longer. Because a size=0 frame IS the normal venue-close signal, this fires on every venue-side close; during a correlated/basket close, N symbols close in one window producing N serial blocking REST calls on the consumer thread. Queued ticker events that drive evaluate_symbols -> plan_risk_exits (the stop_loss/take_profit trigger checks, line 979) wait behind them in self.events, degrading stop-trigger latency exactly when many positions move together. The codebase already recognizes this anti-pattern: the _reconcile_prefetch_loop docstring (ws_risk.py:460-462) explicitly moved positions/orders REST off the consumer thread 'so the slow REST never stalls stop-trigger processing' — but the orphan PnL backfill was left inline on the position-message path. The claim is concrete and verified. Severity medium is correct: it is a latency/efficiency degradation on the hot path under a specific synchronized-move condition, not a correctness/safety bug (a single close is one REST call; the impact scales only with simultaneous orphans).
verdict.fix_notes: The finding is real but neither proposed fix is drop-in safe. Variant 1 (mark orphan closed with a pnl_backfill_pending flag and backfill async via rest_reconcile/the prefetcher) violates the system's single-consumer-thread state-mutation invariant (ws_risk.py:631-635 raises if state is mutated off the consumer thread), so a prefetcher-thread backfill is not directly allowed; it also writes a transient zero-PnL closed row into the ledger that the ws_risk reconcile authority and the demo<->paper<->backtest reconciliation would observe (per project memory, ws_risk is the single reconcile authority and PnL fields feed reconciliation), and adds a new schema field — a behavioral change requiring careful sequencing. Variant 2 (batch all orphans from one frame into a single account-wide get_closed_pnl(settle_coin) sweep, then match per-symbol locally) is the safe DIRECTION and is feasible — get_closed_pnl makes symbol optional (bybit.py:528-530), and records carry per-symbol fields — collapsing N serial paginated calls into 1 while staying synchronous/single-threaded and still emitting fully-priced rows. But it is non-trivial: it requires changing _orphan_close_pnl_backfill/_risk_reconcile_missing_positions to accept a pre-fetched account-wide record set, preserving the per-symbol multi-leg aggregation (M8 logic at event_demo_exits.py:1505-1545), and per-symbol/per-side/since-entry filtering, plus updating the 3 other callers of the backfill (ws_risk.py:1229/1249/1860/1915) or keeping the per-call fallback. Recommend Variant 2 with tests asserting numerical equivalence of the produced backfill rows vs the current per-symbol path, and that pre-push gate (ruff + pytest) passes. Do NOT ship Variant 1 as written.

title: _aggregate_bybit_closures folds two different sleeves' same-symbol short closures into one phantom closure on the shared account
evidence: _aggregate_bybit_closures clusters Bybit closed_pnl rows by (symbol, side) only and merges any rows whose createdTime cluster within window_ms=120_000 (2 min). The docstring assumes 'one position per symbol with a cooldown', valid for a single sleeve. But run_demo_bybit_reconciliation pulls ACCOUNT-WIDE closed_pnl (it queries the union of ledger symbols + all open Bybit positions), and the short + continuous sleeves are BOTH side='short' (close side 'Buy'). If the short sleeve and the continuous sleeve both close the same symbol within 2 minutes (entirely possible: continuous runs a ~2s fast loop + the daily short can exit the same name), the two genuinely-distinct closures merge into ONE cluster: summed closed_size/closed_pnl/fee and a qty-weighted blended entry/exit. The merged closure then mispairs against a single short ledger trade (reconcile_demo_bybit:963-994), corrupting qty_gap/pnl_gap, and the unmerged-away leg disappears so it cannot surface as a real orphan.
impact: reconcile correctness: a real continuous-sleeve closure can be silently absorbed into the short sleeve's pnl_gap, masking a genuine ledger<->venue discrepancy and corrupting the per-pair PnL diff. Reporting-only, but it defeats the cross-check that is supposed to catch position drift on the netted account.
proposed_fix: Scope reconcile_demo_bybit's closed_pnl set to the sleeve actually being reconciled before aggregation: filter Bybit closures whose createdTime falls inside one of THIS ledger's (symbol, side) holding intervals, or pair-then-merge instead of merge-then-pair so a closure that pairs to a different sleeve's trade is excluded from the cluster. At minimum, do not cluster across closures that pair to distinct ledger trade_ids.

verdict.reasoning: Traced the full live code path and the bug is real. run_demo_bybit_reconciliation (reconciliation.py:1259-1331) pulls ACCOUNT-WIDE closed_pnl for the union of short-ledger symbols + open Bybit positions, then reconcile_demo_bybit calls _aggregate_bybit_closures (799-863) which clusters Bybit closures by (symbol, side) ONLY and merges any rows whose createdTime fall within window_ms=120_000. Verified the two preconditions: (1) the short (event/daily) sleeve and the continuous-fade sleeve are BOTH short-direction — continuous_demo.py:749/750 emits trade_side "short" / venue side "Sell" entry + reduce-only "Buy" close, identical to the short sleeve, so both yield original_side="short" at reconciliation.py:931; (2) they run on ONE netted demo account in one-way mode (all place_order calls use the default positionIdx=0; bybit.py never sets a hedge positionIdx), and both short the same top fade decile (D9) of the same universe, so overlapping symbols are entirely possible. The code itself documents this ambiguity (ws_risk.py:1515-1523: "short vs continuous is ambiguous on the netted account"; and _summarize_funding's M7 note at 1108-1111 already scopes funding by symbol to avoid the exact analogous cross-sleeve contamination — yet the closure aggregator does NOT scope by sleeve). When a short-sleeve close and a continuous-sleeve close on the same symbol land within 2 minutes (continuous runs a sub-hourly fast loop; the daily short can exit the same name), both rows have positive timestamps and merge into ONE cluster: summed closed_size/closed_pnl/exec_fee and qty-weighted blended entry/exit (846-862). That merged row pairs to the single short ledger trade (964-994), folding the continuous sleeve's closed_pnl into the short trade's pnl_gap_usdt (1020) and qty_gap (1002), and because the continuous leg is consumed in the merge it never surfaces in orphan_in_bybit (1027-1038). So a genuine continuous-sleeve closure is silently absorbed and the position-drift cross-check is defeated for that case. The docstring's "one position per symbol with a cooldown" invariant is true within a single sleeve but false across sleeves on the shared account. Severity is medium, not high: this is reporting/cross-check integrity only — the reconcile writes a markdown report (run_demo_bybit_reconciliation:1322-1329) and never places orders or mutates the live ledger; and it requires the conjunction of overlapping symbol + sub-2-minute timing, so it is intermittent rather than systemic.
verdict.fix_notes: The finding is real but the proposed fix is NOT side-effect-free and is partly mis-targeted. The accurate disambiguator is already in the codebase: every closing order carries an orderLinkId whose prefix encodes the sleeve (order_link_id.py / continuous_demo.py:36-37: short close vs continuous close = lm-ux- vs lm-ux-c-; decode_entry_order_link_id handles the en- variants). Bybit's closed_pnl rows carry orderLinkId, but reconcile_demo_bybit (941-952) currently does NOT capture it. The robust, minimal fix is: capture orderLinkId in the cleaned closure dict, and (a) in run_demo_bybit_reconciliation/reconcile_demo_bybit drop closures whose closing orderLinkId decodes to a non-short sleeve before aggregation (mirroring _summarize_funding's symbol-scoping), and/or (b) refuse to cluster two closures whose orderLinkIds decode to different sleeves. That is different from the auditor's three suggestions, each of which has a gap: (1) "scope to THIS ledger's (symbol,side) holding intervals" does NOT separate them — a legitimate multi-leg close of the short trade and a continuous close on the same symbol both fall inside the short trade's holding window, so interval filtering can't tell them apart; (2) "pair-then-merge instead of merge-then-pair" is a substantial restructuring that risks regressing the merge's ORIGINAL purpose (folding a single ledger trade's N reduce-only legs into one closure so the extra legs aren't mis-flagged as orphans, per the 802-820 docstring) — pairing un-folded legs reintroduces exactly that orphan-mis-flag, so it is not behavior-preserving; (3) "do not cluster closures that pair to distinct ledger trade_ids" does not fire, because the continuous closure pairs to NO short-ledger trade_id at all (it belongs to the other sleeve), so the rule never triggers on the very leg that needs excluding. Any fix must (i) preserve the legitimate multi-leg-close folding (covered by tests in tests/test_liquidity_migration_reconciliation.py), (ii) gracefully handle closures whose orderLinkId is missing/undecodable (hand-placed/adopted positions) by NOT silently dropping them — surface them rather than hiding a real orphan, matching the existing "don't drop, surface" philosophy at 935-940, and (iii) keep the timestamp-zero guard at 833-837. Recommend implementing the orderLinkId-sleeve-scoping fix with new unit tests for: same-symbol short+continuous close within 2 min (must NOT merge; continuous leg surfaces as orphan or is excluded), genuine multi-leg short close still folds, and missing-orderLinkId closure still surfaces.

title: Continuous (and event/long) ledgers write partition_by=() -> unbounded monolithic part.parquet rewritten on the live hot path under the shared dataset lock
evidence: Every continuous ledger write uses write_dataset(..., partition_by=()) (orders 1058/1130/1261/1268, trades 1132/1270, cycles 1160). With partition_by=() storage writes a single part.parquet at the dataset root; _write_part (storage.py:412-443) does read_parquet(WHOLE file) -> concat -> dedup -> rewrite on EVERY call, i.e. O(N) in cumulative ledger rows per write. The continuous sleeve is sub-hourly (max_active=25, max_hold=48h) with a ~2s fast loop emitting preflight + cover order rows plus per-cycle order/trade rows; the orders dataset in particular grows without bound. The same global per-dataset exclusive_file_lock (storage.py:393) is taken by ws_risk's _read_orders_combined/_read_trades_combined every reconcile pass, so the ever-larger rewrite serializes against the single reconcile authority. Note ws_risk's own event_demo_cycles write was already migrated to partition_by=('date',) for exactly this reason (ws_risk.py:2217-2219 comment: 'partition_by=() made every cycle read+rewrite the whole (unbounded) dataset'), but the continuous/long/event trade+order ledgers were not.
impact: latency/liveness: write + reconcile-read cost on the 60s (and 2s fast-loop) live path grows monotonically with ledger size. Over weeks of a live sub-hourly sleeve the orders parquet becomes multi-MB and each lock-held rewrite stalls both the continuous daemon and the ws_risk stop-trigger reconcile that shares the lock -> risk a missed/late protective exit. Pure execution latency, not a math bug, but it degrades the live risk path.
proposed_fix: Partition the high-churn ledgers by date (partition_by=('date',), deriving date from a ts column) as was already done for event_demo_cycles, so each write only rewrites today's partition and reconcile reads can prune. Keep the trade_id/order_link_id dedup key. Validate reconcile/read paths still glob all partitions (they already do via read_dataset).

verdict.fix_notes: Date partitioning is correct (ts_ms immutable so dedup stays valid) but not side-effect-free: must migrate ALL writers together (continuous_demo.py plus ws_risk._write_rows_routed) and re-partition the existing root part.parquet, else mixed root/partition files yield duplicate rows that corrupt reconcile open-position math.
verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed real. partition_by=() writes a single root part.parquet that _write_part rewrites whole on every call, O(N) in cumulative rows. Continuous trade/order ledgers are append-only and unbounded. ws_risk.rest_reconcile reads them 3-4x per pass under the same per-dataset lock the continuous daemon writes under, so the growing rewrite serializes against the stop-trigger reconcile. event_demo_cycles was already migrated to date partitioning for this exact reason; the trade/order ledgers were not. Gradual latency, not a math bug; medium efficiency.</reasoning>
