title: No min-1h entry-delay enforcement in live — live entry can occur on the same cycle the partial/closed bar appears, unlike the backtest's T+1h fill
evidence: The backtest models entry at `signal_ts + entry_delay_hours*MS_PER_HOUR` (long_native.py:1630) and the sniper window starts at `first_h = max(1, entry_delay_hours)` (long_native.py:1651). The live `_select_long_entry_candidates` checks `live_price <= retrace_threshold` at `now_ms` with NO check that `now_ms >= ts + entry_delay_hours*MS_PER_HOUR`. Combined with finding #1 (partial today bar, whose `ts` is a FUTURE midnight), the deadline branch `now_ms >= deadline_ms` can never fire for a today bar, but the immediate-retrace branch CAN — so a position can be opened the instant a mid-day pump retraces 1%, hours before the backtest's modeled T+1h-after-close fill even begins.
impact: alpha/execution: live entries can lead the validated T+1h fill model, compounding the partial-bar divergence (#1). Even for a properly closed bar the missing floor is harmless, but for the partial bar it materially changes which fills happen.
proposed_fix: Gate entries on `now_ms >= signal_ts_ms + strategy.entry_delay_hours*MS_PER_HOUR` before evaluating the retrace condition, so the live entry window matches the backtest's `[T+entry_delay_h, T+deadline_h]`. Fixing #1 (closed-bar-only) plus this floor restores the backtest's T+1h..T+6h window.

verdict.reasoning:
Traced the full live entry path and the backtest fill model; the divergence is real but conditional on finding #1.

BACKTEST (long_native.py:1630-1674, deployed v11a profile entry_delay_hours=1, fc_sniper_deadline_hours=6): entry_ts_ms = ts + entry_delay_hours*MS_PER_HOUR; the sniper loop runs range(first_h=max(1,entry_delay_hours), deadline_h+1); every candidate fill requires an actual closed bar via bars["by_end"].get(cand_ts). So the backtest never fills before T+1h and never on a not-yet-closed future bar — its window is [T+1h, T+6h] after the signal-bar close.

LIVE (long_native_event_demo.py:880-891): branch-1 `if live_price <= retrace_threshold: entry_reason = "sniper_retrace"` enters at-market this cycle with NO `now_ms >= ts + entry_delay_hours*MS_PER_HOUR` floor. Only the deadline branch checks now_ms (now_ms >= deadline_ms).

PREMISE (finding #1) verified: daily_bars (momentum_signals.py:47-61) filters only hourly_bars >= 20 and stamps ts_ms = day_start_ms + MS_PER_DAY (next/future midnight). A late-day cycle (>=~21:00 UTC) gives today's partial bar >=20 hourly bars, so it survives and emits a FUTURE-midnight ts. The eligible_ts filter (lines 848-851) only enforces the upper bound (now_ms - ts) <= 24h; for a future ts that value is negative and passes — there is no lower-bound / closed-bar guard. _classify_entry is shared with the backtest (imported line 84), so a mid-day pump on the partial bar can classify as fomo_chase. Candidates then flow straight to _execute_long_entries (lines 559-573) with no future-ts guard.

Net: for a partial today bar, now_ms < ts, so the backtest's [T+1h, T+6h] window has not opened, yet the live immediate-retrace branch can fire the instant price retraces ~1% mid-day — a divergence that leads the validated fill. For a properly CLOSED bar, now_ms is already past ts, so now_ms >= ts+1h is naturally true and the missing floor is inert (the finding concedes this).

Severity = medium, not high: the bug only bites in a narrow window — a late-day cycle that leaks a partial today bar (finding #1) which ALSO classifies as FC and whose symbol then retraces mid-day. It is purely an execution/alpha divergence (no crash, no safety/risk impact) and the sleeve runs on demo/paper only. It is a second-order consequence of finding #1; without the partial-bar leak it is harmless.
verdict.fix_notes: Proposed fix (gate entries on `now_ms >= int(ts) + strategy.entry_delay_hours * MS_PER_HOUR` before evaluating the retrace condition, lines 882-891) is correct and side-effect-free for the legitimate closed-bar path. LongNativeConfig.entry_delay_hours exists (long_native.py:294, default 1) and the deployed profile sets it to 1. For a normal CLOSED daily bar, ts is a past midnight and the live cycle runs many hours later, so now_ms >= ts + 1h is already true — the gate is a no-op for real entries. It only suppresses the spurious pre-window entries on a partial today bar (whose ts is a future midnight that now_ms can never reach today), which is exactly the intended behavior and matches the backtest. Recommend implementing the floor with strategy.entry_delay_hours (not a hard-coded 1) so it tracks config. As the finding notes, the cleanest complete remediation pairs this floor with finding #1 (closed-bar-only feature rows); the floor alone already neutralizes the divergence, and fixing #1 makes the floor moot for the partial-bar case while keeping it as defense-in-depth. No new imports needed (MS_PER_HOUR already imported). One caveat: verify the deadline-fallthru branch still behaves as intended once the floor is added — for a closed bar both branches remain reachable as before, so no regression to the validated path.

title: Live universe ranks by CURRENT 24h turnover while the backtest ranks by 90d-median turnover — divergent universe + neutered in-universe gate
evidence: `_build_long_universe` selects the top-50 by CURRENT `turnover24h` (UniverseConfig rank_end=50 on a live ticker snapshot). Only those 50 symbols' klines are fetched. `build_long_features` then recomputes `universe_rank = rank(turnover_median_90d desc)` and `in_universe = universe_rank <= universe_size(50)`. impact: alpha: a second-order backtest/live divergence in which symbols are eligible; the in-universe and top-10-volume gates do less filtering live than in the validated backtest, so live can take names the backtest would have excluded.
proposed_fix: Either rank the live universe by the same trailing-90d-median turnover the backtest uses, or fetch a wider symbol set (e.g. top-150) so the in-universe<=50 / today_volume_rank<=10 gates remain real filters in live. title: ws_risk risk-exit qty = netted account size (plan_risk_exits prefers position.size over trade.qty) over-closes a co-symbol sibling sleeve on the shared account
evidence: plan_risk_exits sets `qty = str(_first_non_empty(position.get('size'), trade.get('qty')))` (event_demo_planning.py:376). _first_non_empty (event_demo.py:2497) returns the FIRST non-empty arg, so the netted Bybit position size wins over this trade's own qty. On the shared demo account the short, long, and continuous sleeves net into ONE position per symbol (one-way mode, get_positions returns a single merged size — bybit.py:493-500). If two sleeves co-hold symbol X same-direction (short sleeve qty=100, continuous qty=50 → netted 150), a risk stop on the short sleeve's trade plans a reduce-only Buy of qty=150 (the netted size). _execute_risk_exits:714 and ws_exit (ws_risk.py:1137) both take `exit_plan.qty` first, so they submit the full 150. The venue caps reduce-only at the live size, so BOTH sleeves' 150 is flattened by one sleeve's stop. The continuous sleeve's position vanishes from Bybit while its ledger still shows it open → it then surfaces as a (symbol-keyed, see reconcile-core-1) orphan/untracked. The account-wide entry exclusion (continuous_demo.py:1085 cooldown=held|live_position_symbols|...) is the ONLY guard against co-holding, and it is a per-cycle netted snapshot shared across 3 independent daemons — two daemons in the same minute can both see X unheld and both enter, defeating it.
impact: money/exposure: one sleeve's stop silently flattens another sleeve's same-symbol exposure; the victim sleeve's ledger over-reports open exposure; net book vs venue diverges; the over-closed sleeve realizes an unintended exit at the stopping sleeve's price.
proposed_fix: On a shared/netted account, risk exits must size to the TRADE's own qty, not the netted position size: change plan_risk_exits to prefer trade.qty (or min(trade.qty, position.size)) when more than one sleeve root is configured, OR gate the position.size preference behind a 'single-sleeve account' flag. Long-term: track per-sleeve intended qty and never submit a reduce-only larger than this trade's recorded qty.

verdict.reasoning:
Code facts all verified. plan_risk_exits (event_demo_planning.py:376) sets qty = _first_non_empty(position.get("size"), trade.get("qty")); _first_non_empty (event_demo.py:2497) returns the first non-empty arg so the netted position size wins. ws_risk reads a COMBINED cross-sleeve ledger (ws_risk.py:425-426,513) and evaluate_symbols->plan_risk_exits (ws_risk.py:976-984) iterates all three sleeves' open trades against self.state.positions_by_symbol, which is the netted per-symbol snapshot (_active_position_by_symbol maps each symbol to one merged position; one-way mode, position_idx=0 default in bybit.py:644). ws_exit (ws_risk.py:1137) and rest_exit take exit_plan.qty first. So IF two SHORT-direction sleeves (short-event + continuous; both Sell) co-hold the same symbol, they net-ADD (e.g. 100+50=150), and a stop on one sleeve's trade submits a reduce-only Buy sized to the netted 150, flattening BOTH sleeves' exposure. The victim sleeve realizes an unintended exit at the stopper's price and its ledger transiently over-reports until reconcile. This is a genuine exposure/accounting hazard, so is_real=true.

HOWEVER the severity is LOW, not high: (1) Co-holding is structurally prevented by an account-wide entry exclusion present in BOTH sleeves — the short sleeve's _filter_live_position_entry_orders (event_demo.py:1985) and continuous's cooldown = held|live_position_symbols|... (continuous_demo.py:1085) both drop any candidate already showing a live netted position. The ONLY way to co-hold is a same-snapshot entry race between two independent daemons, and fills confirm within seconds (fast poll 0.05s) so the next cycle's snapshot picks the position up — a narrow window. (2) reduce_only=True (ws_risk.py:1182) bounds the damage to at most the netted size: no over-flip, no oversize, exactly as the design doc states (event_demo_planning.py:250-251). (3) It SELF-HEALS: the over-closed sleeve's row is orphan-closed next reconcile with exit_reason=bybit_position_missing and PnL backfilled from get_closed_pnl, keyed on (symbol, side) (event_demo_exits.py:1357, event_demo.py:2449-2477) — no permanent venue/ledger divergence. Bounded + race-gated + self-reconciling = low.

Note the deliberate asymmetry the auditor under-weighted: the peer cadence-exit planner plan_demo_exits (event_demo_planning.py:353) uses trade.qty, while plan_risk_exits intentionally prefers position.size because on a netted account the risk daemon's job on a stop is to close everything the venue shows for that symbol (also the source-of-truth qty for ADOPTED positions and stale/partial-fill ledger rows). Tests pin this (test_plan_risk_exits_uses_live_position_price_for_stops, 9 passed).
verdict.fix_notes: The proposed immediate fix is NOT side-effect-free and should not be applied as-is. Preferring trade.qty or min(trade.qty, position.size) on the risk-exit path introduces an UNDER-close hazard on the safety-critical stop path: position.size is intentionally the authoritative venue size, used for adopted positions (_build_adopted_trade sets qty=position size) and for stale/partial-fill/stop-repair ledger rows where trade.qty under-records the real venue size. min() would then leave a residual unprotected position open past its stop — a strictly worse risk outcome than the rare cross-sleeve over-close it tries to prevent. The existing test test_plan_risk_exits_uses_live_position_price_for_stops pins the position.size-preference and would need changing. A 'single-sleeve account flag' gate is also fragile: the deployed demo account IS multi-sleeve (3 short-capable sleeves net), so that branch would just disable the safer behavior in production. The only sound remedy is the auditor's own long-term suggestion: track per-sleeve intended qty and never submit a reduce-only larger than this trade's recorded qty — but that requires per-sleeve position attribution that get_positions cannot provide on a netted one-way account, so it needs a per-sleeve qty ledger reconciliation, not a one-line qty swap. Given the bug is low severity (race-gated, reduce-only-bounded, self-reconciling), the right call is to keep the current behavior and, if anything, strengthen the same-minute cross-daemon entry-race guard (e.g. a shared just-submitted-entry symbol lock) rather than touch the stop-sizing.

title: all_trades holds the full historical closed-trade ledger and is fully materialized via .to_dicts() on every exit/fill on the latency-critical path; _tag_sleeve_from_trades does it twice per call
evidence: self.state.all_trades is reloaded every rest_reconcile from the combined ledger (ws_risk.py:1331 via _read_trades_combined), which is read_dataset over the entire per-sleeve trades datasets INCLUDING all historical CLOSED trades (closed rows are never pruned from the parquet — only the in-memory log lists are pruned, _prune_state_logs/_prune_closed_order_state, not all_trades). Every exit fill rebuilds a dict over the whole frame: record_tracked_exit_stream_fill `trades = {... for row in self.state.all_trades.to_dicts()}` (ws_risk.py:807); ws_exit `trade_lookup = {... all_trades.to_dicts()}` (ws_risk.py:1132); and _tag_sleeve_from_trades materializes all_trades.to_dicts() TWICE in two separate loops (ws_risk.py:1084 and 1088) on every exit/repair submission. After months of forward demo this is thousands of closed rows → Python dicts per WS fill, on the stop path.
impact: growing latency + memory churn on the live exit hot path; cost scales with cumulative trade count, not open positions — unbounded growth on a long-lived daemon.
proposed_fix: Build the trade_id→row and symbol→sleeve lookups ONCE per cycle (or maintain incremental dicts) instead of per-fill; in _tag_sleeve_from_trades do a single to_dicts() and build both indices in one pass. Filter to open_trades for the exit-fill lookups where only open trades are relevant. Consider keeping all_trades trimmed to open + recently-closed in memory and reading closed history only on demand.

verdict.reasoning:
The factual core of the finding is verified against the code. `self.state.all_trades` is reloaded every `rest_reconcile` via `_read_trades_combined` -> `_read_combined` -> `read_dataset(root, dataset)` (ws_risk.py:1331, 412-416, 391), which reads the entire per-sleeve trades parquet with no status filter. Closed rows are never pruned: `_write_part` (storage.py:412-443) dedupes by trade_id (DATASET_KEYS) and keeps the freshest version — a closed trade is updated in place to status="closed" and stays forever; the in-memory pruners `_prune_state_logs` (2062) and `_prune_closed_order_state` (2077) touch only telemetry logs and per-order-link maps, never `all_trades`. So `all_trades` grows monotonically with cumulative trade count.

The three materializations are confirmed on the exit-submission path: `record_tracked_exit_stream_fill` (807), `ws_exit` (1132), and `_tag_sleeve_from_trades` which calls `.to_dicts()` TWICE in two separate loops (1084 build trade_index, 1088 build symbol_index). A single `submit_exit` -> `ws_exit` + `record_exit_submission_result` -> `_tag_sleeve_from_trades` triggers three full-frame to_dicts() over the entire historical ledger.

So the bug is REAL as described. However the severity is overstated. (1) These run at exit-event frequency, not the per-WS-message hot loop. (2) Cost is O(cumulative_trades) per exit; for a small-universe short demo live ~11 days (since 2026-05-22) the realistic row count is low hundreds, not "thousands" — that figure is a multi-month worst-case extrapolation, not current state. (3) to_dicts() over a few hundred-to-few-thousand rows is single-digit milliseconds; there is NO correctness impact, no stop is missed, no position is mis-routed. It is a genuine but minor scalability wart, not a medium-grade live risk. Hence low, not medium.
verdict.fix_notes:
The fix is PARTIALLY safe — split it:

SAFE and high-value (do this): Collapse the two `to_dicts()` passes in `_tag_sleeve_from_trades` (1082-1092) into ONE. Build trade_index and symbol_index in a single iteration over `self.state.all_trades.to_dicts()`. Must preserve symbol_index FIRST-WINS semantics (the `if sym and sleeve and sym not in symbol_index` guard at 1091) — iterating once in the same row order with the same guard reproduces it exactly. No test pins the double-pass, so this is side-effect-free. Likewise, hoisting a per-cycle trade_id->row lookup so `record_tracked_exit_stream_fill`/`ws_exit` don't each rebuild it is safe IF the dict is rebuilt whenever all_trades changes (it is mutated mid-cycle by `_upsert_rows` at 870/1047/1288/1412 etc.), so a naive "build once per rest_reconcile" cache would go STALE between an exit and a subsequent fill within the same cycle — must invalidate on every all_trades mutation, or it introduces a real bug.

RISKY (do NOT apply blindly): The suggestions to "filter to open_trades for the exit-fill lookups" and "keep all_trades trimmed to open + recently-closed, read closed history on demand" can regress correctness. `record_tracked_exit_stream_fill` (813) deliberately inspects status=="closed" to catch the WS-then-REST double-close race; trimming closed rows out of all_trades removes the row the guard relies on. Other consumers (cooldown, reporting, ledger PnL) also read closed rows. Trimming all_trades is NOT side-effect-free and should not be done as part of this efficiency fix.

Recommendation: apply only the single-pass `_tag_sleeve_from_trades` change (zero risk, captures most of the cited waste). Treat the trimming/caching as a separate, test-gated change.

title: Test gap: no coverage for netted same-symbol over-close, symbol-only orphan-flip, or evidence-less WS size=0 close — the three highest-blast-radius reconcile failures are untested
evidence: The ws_risk suite tests the adopt/flatten (untracked) direction (test_liquidity_migration_ws_risk_dual_sleeve.py:157,190), the REST transient-failure C1 guard (test_liquidity_migration_ws_risk.py:3350), and the ledger_read_error fail-closed flatten guard (test:1395). verdict.reasoning:
This is a TEST-GAP finding, not a live-code bug, so "is_real" = whether the named scenarios are genuinely untested. I traced both reconcile paths and the full test surface. Of the three sub-claims, only one is a clean, material, untested gap:

Every _risk_reconcile_missing_positions test passes position_by_symbol={} (lines 1297/1315/1463), so the same-symbol short→long flip on the WS reconcile authority is genuinely untested. On the WS daemon a short→long flip keeps the phantom short open — a real divergence with no failing test. The auditor correctly conceded "the side-aware helper exists but is only exercised on the cycle path."

(a) Netted over-close — NOT real as described. Risk exits size to `exit_plan.qty or trade.qty` (per-trade qty) with reduce_only=True (event_demo_exits.py:714, 731). There is no netted-position-size pathway in exit sizing, so the over-close bug described cannot occur; the proposed test (1) would pass trivially against current code and documents a non-risk.

The behavior IS exercised: test at line 2361 uses the base FakePrivateClient which has NO get_closed_pnl, so _orphan_close_pnl_backfill returns {} and the trade closes at zero-PnL via on_position_message. That close path is tested. The WS path deliberately uses require_evidence=False (close-on-absence) with the position_error guard as its only safety — documented at event_demo_exits.py:1410-1417 and config default at event_demo.py:86-92. Net: one genuine, material untested gap (b); the other two are mis-characterized. Severity downgraded medium→low: it is a test gap (no current incorrect behavior demonstrated), and the one real gap concerns a rare same-symbol cross-side-flip on a shared netted account, not an everyday path.

title: PIT symbol_age_days / pit_age_days computed from signal STAMP date, not the trading day (date(ts_ms-1ms)) -> +1 day age offset feeding the live age300 gate
evidence: tradable_membership_flag is correctly keyed on trading_day_expr('ts_ms') = date(ts_ms-1ms) (the 2026-05-30 fix, _common.py:85-96). But symbol_age_days and pit_age_days are computed as pl.col('date') - first_manifest_date, where 'date' is the STAMP date pl.from_epoch(ts_ms).strftime (the day AFTER the bar) set at line 494-495/531-543, while first_manifest_date is a manifest archive date (a true trading day, archive CSVs named by the day they cover). So age = stamp_date - launch_trading_day is +1 day vs the consistent trading_day - launch_trading_day. This is the live SELECTION gate (`age300`, pit_age_days_min=300). It is internally consistent (live and backtest share this function so they agree with each other), so it is NOT alpha-faking; it is a 1-day definitional imprecision on a 300-day threshold and relates to the 'age300 live!=backtest definition' debt in STATE.md.
impact: alpha (minor): the effective age gate is ~299 trading days, not 300, by a fixed 1-day stamp/trading-day offset. Negligible economically; flagged for definitional correctness because age300 is the deployed gate and the codebase elsewhere went to lengths to key membership on the trading day.
proposed_fix: Compute age from the trading day to match membership: use trading_day_expr('ts_ms') in place of pl.col('date') in the two age subtractions, so age = trading_day - first_manifest_date. Add to tests/test_pit_membership_trading_day.py.

verdict.reasoning:
The code-level observation is real and reproducible. In _attach_event_archive_membership (volume_events_features.py:521-543), the membership flag correctly keys on the trading day trading_day_expr('ts_ms') = date(ts_ms-1ms) (the 2026-05-30 fix, _common.py:96), but symbol_age_days/pit_age_days are computed as pl.col('date') - first_manifest_date, where 'date' is the STAMP date date(ts_ms) created at line 494-495 and first_manifest_date is a true trading day. I confirmed first_manifest_date is a trading day: the archive scrape parses CSV filenames {SYMBOL}{YYYY-MM-DD}.csv where the date is the day the trades occurred (archive_manifest.py:307-322), and the v5-listing synthesis uses launch_date=date(launch_ms) as coverage_start (archive_manifest.py:244-265). build_volume_features stamps ts_ms = day_start_ms + aggregation_ms (volume_features.py:104, stamp convention) and emits no 'date' column, so line 494's guard fires and 'date' = stamp date. I reproduced the offset directly: a symbol whose true trading-day age is 300 gets pit_age_days=301; equivalently a 299-trading-day symbol passes the >=300 gate, so the effective BACKTEST gate is 299 trading days, not 300. The math direction in the finding is correct.

However, the auditor materially mischaracterizes the SCOPE. The finding repeatedly frames this as 'the live SELECTION gate (age300)... fed by the stamp date' and claims 'live and backtest share this function so they agree.' That is FALSE for the live path. The live demo path (event_demo_data._build_demo_features:600-614) calls _enriched_event_features with an EMPTY manifest and then DROPS the manifest-derived symbol_age_days/pit_age_days and OVERWRITES them with the universe's listing_age_days = (snapshot_ts_ms - launch_time_ms)/MS_PER_DAY (universe.py:92) — a continuous launch-timestamp-based age entirely independent of this stamp-vs-manifest subtraction. So the cited offset affects the BACKTEST path only; the deployed live age300 gate is NOT fed by it. This is the backtest sub-component of the already-tracked 'age300 live!=backtest definition' methodology debt in STATE.md:72.

So: real backtest-side definitional imprecision (+1 day on a 300-day threshold, ~0.33%), internally consistent within the backtest, not a look-ahead, not alpha-faking. Low/methodology is the correct severity; the finding's own 'live and backtest agree' justification is the one factual error, but it does not change the severity classification.
verdict.fix_notes:
The proposed fix (substitute trading_day_expr('ts_ms') for pl.col('date') in the two age subtractions at lines 531-543) is type-correct: trading_day_expr returns pl.Date, first_manifest_date is parsed to pl.Date, so Date-Date -> Duration -> .dt.total_days() works, and it correctly aligns the backtest age to the trading day. It does NOT break the existing tests/test_pit_membership_trading_day.py, which only assert the 'date' column stays the stamp date (2026-05-30) and the membership flag — both unchanged by the fix.

But it is NOT side-effect-free. It is a BEHAVIORAL change to the backtest selection set: it shifts every age boundary by 1 day for BOTH pit_age_days (the age300 gate, volume_events.py:1240) AND symbol_age_days (the top_volume/leadership/shelf min-age filters in volume_events_filters.py:258/287/311). Under this repo's rules (AGENTS.md pre-registration + CLAUDE.md 'profile change is a hard line'), shifting which symbols pass age300 in a backtest is an alpha/signal-touching change that requires a pre-registration entry and goes through the forward-demo arbiter — not a silent merge. Additionally, the fix narrows ONE discrepancy but does NOT actually make backtest age equal live age: live uses listing_age_days = (snapshot_ts_ms - launch_time_ms)/day (continuous, launch-timestamp-based), whereas even the fixed backtest age is trading_day - first_manifest_trading_day (integer, manifest-derived). So the 'live!=backtest definition' debt persists after the fix. title: Live ledger net_return is GROSS of fees and funding while the backtest net_return is net-of-cost — inconsistent accounting fed into the circuit breaker
evidence: _execute_continuous_exits computes net_return = gtr * nw where gtr=_trade_return(entry,exit) and nw=notional/equity — NO subtraction of entry_fee_usdt/exit_fee_usdt and NO funding (lines 782-787). The backtest (continuous_events._additive_summary) reports net_return WITH cost_return and funding_return baked in. The live circuit-breaker classifier _recent_adverse_exit_count keys 'adverse' partly on net_return<0 (lines 639-640), so a trade that is a small gross winner but a net loser after the ~45bps round-trip + funding is NOT counted as adverse, weakening the squeeze defense; and any internal use of the live net_return overstates realized PnL by the round-trip cost.
impact: Telemetry/accounting: live ledger net_return overstates PnL (alpha optimism in any dashboard reading it); the adverse-cover count that drives the entry-pause circuit breaker is biased low. Reconciliation is OK because it compares gross_trade_return and accounts fees separately, but the headline net_return field is misleading.
proposed_fix: Subtract entry_fee_usdt+exit_fee_usdt (and a funding estimate where available) from the live net_return, or rename the field to gross_net_return and compute a true net_return for parity with the engine; ensure the circuit breaker's adverse test matches the engine's net_return<0 semantics on a like-for-like (cost-inclusive) basis.

verdict.reasoning:
The factual core of the finding is correct, but severity is overstated and it is mischaracterized as a continuous-specific bug.

CONFIRMED FACTS:
- continuous_demo.py:780-784 computes live net_return = gtr * nw (gross_trade_return * notional_weight), with NO subtraction of entry_fee_usdt/exit_fee_usdt and no funding. Fees are stored separately in exit_fee_usdt (line 783).
- The backtest engine (volume_events.py:1500-1502, surfaced via continuous_events._simulate_indexed_trade) computes net_return = gross_return + cost_return + funding_return, i.e. cost-inclusive. So the live net_return field equals the engine's GROSS_return, not the engine's net_return. The naming is genuinely inconsistent.
- The live circuit breaker _recent_adverse_exit_count (continuous_demo.py:636-641) keys 'adverse' on exit_reason in {stop_approach, failed_fade} OR net_return<0, while the engine's validation (continuous_events.py:437) keys adverse on its cost-inclusive net_return<0. continuous_events.py:106-107 explicitly claims these are like-for-like proxies, so the gross-vs-net gap is a real semantic mismatch between live and engine.

WHY SEVERITY IS LOW, NOT MEDIUM:
- This is a REPO-WIDE LIVE CONVENTION, not a continuous-sleeve accounting bug. event_demo_exits.py:345, 577, 830, 1538 (SHORT event sleeve, incl. the B3 closed-PnL backfill) and long_native_event_demo.py:1212 all use the identical formula net_return = gross_trade_return * notional_weight with fees tracked in *_fee_usdt. Even the orphan/closedPnl backfill recomputes from price, not from Bybit's net closedPnl. So the field is a uniformly-named 'notional-weighted gross', not a corrupted value.
- The circuit-breaker weakening is real but narrow: the dominant correlated-squeeze footprint (stop_approach / failed_fade cuts) is caught by the exit_reason branch regardless of the net/gross gap. The only missed trades are gross-positive-but-net-negative exits via left_decile/breakeven (sub-~45bps gross winners) — a thin band, and during an actual squeeze those names get cut via stop_approach/failed_fade anyway.
- Reconciliation is unaffected: reconciliation.py:595 compares gross_trade_return (and recomputes gross from prices at 596-600); net_return is carried (line 123) but never compared. The auditor concedes this.

So: a real, low-impact telemetry-naming + circuit-breaker-proxy inconsistency, not a data-integrity/accounting corruption.
verdict.fix_notes:
The proposed fix (subtract entry_fee_usdt+exit_fee_usdt + funding from the live net_return) is NOT side-effect-free and does not achieve true parity:

1. Cross-sleeve inconsistency: net_return = gross_trade_return * notional_weight is a repo-wide live convention (event_demo_exits.py:345/577/830/1538, long_native_event_demo.py:1212, B3 backfill). Changing ONLY the continuous sleeve's net_return makes continuous net_return mean something different from the event/long sleeves, breaking any cross-sleeve aggregation (trade_lifecycle.py basket/win-rate aggregation, scripts/alpha_sweep.py:629-689 which sum net_return). To be consistent the change would have to touch all sleeves at once — a much larger, riskier edit.

2. It would not even produce true engine parity: live trades carry ACTUAL per-fill fees (exit_fee_usdt) while the engine charges a FLAT round_trip_cost_bps (volume_events.py:1500). Subtracting realized fees into live net_return makes it diverge from the engine's modeled-cost net_return in the opposite direction, so the 'like-for-like' goal is still not met.

3. Note exit_fee_usdt is a USDT amount while net_return is a fraction-of-equity; the fix as literally stated (subtract fee_usdt from a return fraction) is unit-inconsistent and would need fee_usdt/equity_usdt scaling — easy to get wrong and silently corrupt the ledger.

A safer, narrower fix that matches the stated intent: leave the net_return field convention alone (preserve cross-sleeve consistency and dashboards) and instead make ONLY the circuit-breaker's adverse test cost-aware — e.g. compare (net_return - modeled_round_trip_frac) < 0, using the same round-trip-bps the engine uses, so the live adverse set matches the engine's net_return<0 semantics like-for-like. Alternatively, rename the field to gross_net_return / notional_weighted_gross_return across ALL sleeves in one coordinated change and add a separately-computed true net_return. Both are larger than the one-spot edit implied and should be test-gated against reconciliation + the circuit-breaker tests before any push (the live VPS auto-deploys on push to main).

title: Entry decile (confirmed +1h) and exit decile (live intra-hour) disagree, so a freshly-entered name can be left_decile-covered within the same hour
evidence: Entries are selected from entry_state=build_confirmed_entry_state (confirmed bar, +entry_confirm_delay_hours) while exits' left_decile uses live_state=build_live_continuous_state (synthetic intra-hour bar). The two panels can disagree at the boundary: a name in D9 on the confirmed deciding bar may sit below exit_decile_min (decile - exit_decile_buffer) on the live intra-hour decile in the same cycle, so plan_continuous_exits fires left_decile on a position opened seconds earlier. The 30-min reentry cooldown + the hysteresis buffer=1 limit churn but do not prevent the immediate same-cycle/next-cycle whipsaw.
impact: Fee churn and potential immediate flat round-trips on boundary names; mild drag, not a money-loss or ledger-corruption bug.
proposed_fix: Either gate left_decile on the SAME confirmed-bar decile used for entry (so entry and state-exit share a panel), or suppress left_decile for a position younger than ~1 bar / the entry_confirm_delay window.

verdict.reasoning:
The mechanism is real. ENTRIES select from build_confirmed_entry_state (continuous_demo.py:1046-1048), whose decile is the confirmed deciding bar at deciding_ts = cur_ts - (1+entry_confirm_delay_hours)*1h (with the default delay=1, that is cur_ts - 2h; line 232). EXITS use live_state = build_live_continuous_state (line 1065-1067), whose decile is the current intra-hour bar with a synthetic live-price bar (line 188-209). The two panels reference different timestamps and can genuinely disagree. plan_continuous_exits fires left_decile when decile_by_symbol.get(symbol, -1) < exit_decile_min, where exit_decile_min = decile - exit_decile_buffer = 9 - 1 = 8 (line 551, 564). So a name that was D9 on the confirmed bar 2h ago can be at D7-or-below on the live cross, firing left_decile on a position opened in the previous cycle. There is NO minimum-hold/young-position guard before left_decile in plan_continuous_exits (lines 557-570). The reentry_cooldown (_recent_exit_cooldown_symbols, line 601) only blocks RE-ENTRY of a closed name (it filters status=='closed'), so it does not prevent the immediate exit. The hysteresis buffer only blocks a 1-decile wobble (D9->D8 held; tests line 441-466 pin this).

Two corrections to the auditor's claim: (1) a SAME-cycle whipsaw is impossible — open_trades is read at line 1051 and passed to plan_continuous_exits at 1066 BEFORE entries are selected/written (entries write at line 1132), so a name entered this cycle is not in this cycle's exit pass. The earliest exit is the NEXT cycle (~60s later). The auditor hedges with 'same-cycle/next-cycle', so the next-cycle claim holds. (2) The trigger requires a genuine >=2-decile drop on the live cross (D9->D7), a substantial cross-sectional move, not noise.

Severity is LOW, matching the auditor's own impact line (fee churn / mild drag, not money-loss or ledger corruption). Crucially, left_decile is by design the strategy's PROFIT-TAKING state exit (config comment lines 95-98: "leave-the-decile is a PROFIT exit a squeezing name never triggers"), so an early left_decile cover is the sleeve correctly recognizing the fade edge decayed — at a poor fee/round-trip granularity. The cost is bounded to one extra maker/taker round-trip on boundary names that move >=2 deciles within ~2h of entry, a rare and small drag.
verdict.fix_notes: Neither proposed fix is drop-in / side-effect-free, because both alter a deployed (demo/paper) sleeve's exit behavior, which is alpha-adjacent under repo rules (any exit-logic change is EXPLORATORY and must be pre-registered + forward-demo arbitered, not patched as a correctness fix). Option 1 (gate left_decile on the same confirmed-bar decile as entry) is the riskier one: it would decouple the state-exit from the live tick-driven panel that the codebase DELIBERATELY keeps live for squeeze protection (comments lines 45, 66, 511-512) and would change exit timing for ALL positions, not just fresh ones — a material alpha change. Option 2 (suppress left_decile for a position younger than ~1 bar / the entry_confirm_delay window) is the targeted, lower-risk choice and aligns with the existing anti-thrash intent: it would only delay the profit-state exit for freshly-opened names while leaving the protective exits (breakeven/stop_approach/failed_fade/max_hold) fully active. But even option 2 is not provably neutral — it slightly extends hold on a young name whose fade has genuinely decayed, and it touches deployed exit logic, so it needs a pre-registration entry + the test suite + forward-demo validation before shipping. Recommended path: implement option 2 behind the existing config (e.g., a min_hold_bars_before_left_decile guard, default 0 = current behavior) so it is opt-in and the np.allclose/test gate stays green, then validate on demo. Given low severity (bounded fee drag, no correctness/money-loss exposure), doing nothing is also a defensible choice.

title: No test pins the same-hour re-entry trade_id/orderLinkId uniqueness; the continuous ledger collision class is uncovered
evidence: The continuous tests cover reentry_cooldown, hysteresis, the panel cache equivalence, link encode/decode, and entry/exit execution, but none exercises a cover-then-re-enter within the same deciding-bar hour, so the continuous-2 collision (duplicate trade_id dropping the closed row on storage dedup, and the duplicate orderLinkId) is unguarded. The reconciliation tests vary entry_ts_ms but trade_id is keyed on signal_ts_ms, so they never collide.
impact: A money/ledger-affecting collision class (continuous-2) can regress silently.
proposed_fix: Add a test: open symbol S at deciding bar T; cover (left_decile/protective); re-enter S in the same wall-clock hour after the cooldown lifts; assert two distinct trade_ids, two distinct entry orderLinkIds, and that both the closed and the new-open rows survive a write_dataset→read_dataset round-trip.

VERIFIED REAL test-gap. I traced the full collision path and reproduced it concretely.

Mechanics (all in liquidity_migration/continuous_demo.py): signal_ts is keyed purely on the wall-clock hour — `cur_hour_ts = (cycle_now_ms // MS_PER_HOUR) * MS_PER_HOUR` then `signal_ts = cur_hour_ts - 2*MS_PER_HOUR` for the default entry_confirm_delay_hours=1 (lines 1110-1113), with no sub-hour resolution. Both `trade_id = f"{strategy_id}-{symbol}-{signal_ts_ms}"` (line 884) and `entry_link = _continuous_order_link_id(..., signal_ts_ms=signal_ts_ms)` (line 838) are derived solely from signal_ts_ms. So a cover-then-reenter of the same symbol within the SAME wall-clock hour produces an IDENTICAL trade_id and entry orderLinkId.

Reachability: the only re-entry guards are held_symbols, live positions/orders, and the 30-min `_recent_exit_cooldown_symbols` (lines 1084-1089). NONE blocks re-entry based on an existing CLOSED trade_id. A cover at minute m<=29 with cooldown lifting at m+30<=59 lets a same-hour re-entry through (e.g. cover :04, re-enter :35). With reentry_cooldown_minutes=0 (a supported config) it collides even same-cycle.

Impact confirmed: storage dedups `continuous_fade_demo_trades` on ("trade_id",) and `_orders` on ("order_link_id",) (storage.py DATASET_KEYS lines 139-140), via `unique(subset=keys, keep="last")` after `sort("updated_at_ms")` (storage.py 432-434). I reproduced it: wrote open#1 -> cover (closed, net_return=0.05) -> same-hour re-enter (open#2, same trade_id). Final ledger collapsed to ONE row = the new open; the closed row carrying realized PnL was DROPPED. So the underlying continuous-2 collision is real and money/ledger-affecting.

Test-gap confirmed: the continuous suite (42 tests, green) covers reentry_cooldown, hysteresis, panel-cache equivalence, link encode/decode, and entry/exit execution, but NONE exercises a same-hour cover-then-reenter. The reconciliation tests (test_liquidity_migration_reconciliation.py:595-638) pair two SEPARATE ledgers' rows via signal_ts and never collide a single ledger on trade_id — exactly as the finding states. So the collision class is genuinely unguarded by tests and could regress silently.

Severity low is appropriate for the test-gap framing (this is missing coverage, not a newly-introduced live regression); the underlying continuous-2 collision is the more serious item that this gap leaves unprotected.
verdict.fix_notes:
The proposed fix (add a test asserting two DISTINCT trade_ids, two DISTINCT entry orderLinkIds, and both closed+new-open rows surviving a write->read round-trip) is NOT a safe, drop-in green test against the current code. I demonstrated that the live code produces IDENTICAL trade_id and orderLinkId for a same-hour re-entry, and the trade_id dedup collapses the closed row. So the proposed assertions would FAIL on the current production code — the test would go RED, not green.

In other words, the proposed test implicitly requires a PRODUCTION fix to continuous-2 first (give the trade_id/orderLinkId a per-entry uniqueness component — e.g. suffix with the entry attempt index or entry_ts_ms, the same pattern `_risk_order_link_id`/`_split_order_link_id` already use for sub-order uniqueness in order_link_id.py), which the finding does not include. As written, the fix is incomplete.

Two correct ways to land this without contradiction: (a) write the test as a REGRESSION-CAPTURE that asserts the CURRENT (buggy) collapse behavior, documenting the known gap (safe, green, but doesn't fix anything); or (b) first fix continuous-2 in production by adding a per-entry suffix to trade_id and entry orderLinkId so a same-hour re-entry is a distinct identity, THEN add the proposed uniqueness+round-trip test (this is the real fix). Note option (b) must keep ws_risk's `decode_entry_order_link_id` and the deterministic VPS-rebuild reconstruction working — any new orderLinkId suffix must stay within Bybit's 36-char cap and remain decodable, so it is NOT a trivially side-effect-free change.

title: Cross-sleeve same-symbol exclusion has a same-minute race (long vs short/continuous net on the one-way account)
evidence: Same-symbol exclusion relies on `_filter_by_symbol_set(candidates, live_position_symbols)` and `live_entry_order_symbols`, both derived from the account-wide REST/WS snapshot taken at cycle start. If the short or continuous sleeve submits a SHORT in SYMBOL in the same ~60s window (after this cycle's snapshot, before its entry), the long sleeve sees no existing position/order and can enter a LONG in the same SYMBOL. On a one-way (netted) account a long and a short in the same symbol net against each other, corrupting both sleeves' position accounting until ws_risk reconciles. Overlap is rare (FC long universe vs short fade universe) but not impossible.
impact: ledger: transient same-symbol long+short netting across sleeves on the shared account → per-sleeve position drift until reconcile; small but real correctness exposure on the netted account.
proposed_fix: Cross-check sibling-sleeve OPEN+PENDING ledgers (short/continuous trades+orders) in addition to the account-wide live snapshot before entry, and/or have ws_risk own a single account-wide symbol-reservation table the sleeves consult. Add a test simulating a sibling-sleeve pending order in the same symbol.

verdict.reasoning:
The code path is real and traceable. (1) The cross-sleeve same-symbol exclusion in the long cycle is snapshot-based: live_position_symbols / live_entry_order_symbols are derived once at cycle start from an account-wide REST/WS snapshot (long_native_event_demo.py:402-416), then consumed at entry filtering ~lines 533-534. (2) Entries fire much later in the same cycle (line 559), after klines download + feature build + exits — a multi-second wall-clock gap, so the snapshot is genuinely stale by entry time. (3) The local pending-order check (_filter_pending_long_entries, line 522) reads ONLY the long sleeve's own orders ledger; it does NOT consult sibling (short/continuous) ledgers — the only cross-sleeve guard is the stale live snapshot. (4) The three sleeves take DISTINCT locks (long_native_event_demo_cycle.lock vs event_demo_ledger.lock vs continuous_demo_cycle.lock), so they run concurrently with no serialization. (5) The account is one-way (position_idx=0 default in bybit.set_trading_stop / order placement), so a long and a short in the same symbol DO net against each other. (6) The universes can overlap (long FC universe and short fade universe both draw from the same liquid-coin pool). Thus a sibling SHORT submitted after the long snapshot but before the long entry is invisible to the long cycle, which can then open a LONG in the same symbol → transient netting on the shared one-way account. The codebase itself anticipates exactly this flip (event_demo.py:2453 comment: "if a short closes and a long is opened on the same symbol ... two daemons sharing an account"), and the shared-account architecture memo names "account-wide same-symbol exclusion (Rule A)" as snapshot-based — confirming the mechanism and its snapshot dependency.

However severity is genuinely LOW, matching the auditor's own framing. The trigger requires a rare conjunction: universe overlap on the SAME symbol + simultaneous fresh entry signals in BOTH sleeves + overlapping entry windows + the sibling firing precisely in the post-snapshot/pre-entry slice. The impact is transient: ws_risk is the documented single reconcile authority (reads all sleeve ledgers, keys positions by (symbol, side), backfills real venue PnL on orphan-close, routes writes per sleeve) and self-heals the drift on its next reconcile pass. There is no persistent ledger corruption, no fund loss, and no look-ahead/PIT correctness issue — just briefly reduced net exposure and short-lived per-sleeve position-accounting drift until reconcile. So this is a real but small correctness exposure on the netted account, not a high/medium-severity defect.
verdict.fix_notes: The proposed fix is directionally correct but NOT a clean, side-effect-free drop-in. (a) Cross-checking sibling OPEN+PENDING ledgers (short event_demo_* + continuous continuous_fade_demo_*) inside the long entry path adds new cross-root reads on a hot, latency-sensitive path where the long sleeve already runs a deliberately throttled REST budget; it introduces a new failure mode (sibling-ledger read error) that must be designed fail-closed-or-open explicitly, mirroring ws_risk._note_ledger_read_error, or it can wrongly block long entries. (b) It only NARROWS the race, it does not close it: the sibling writes its order row via preflight BEFORE place_order (event_demo.py:775), so a ledger cross-check would catch an already-flushed sibling order — but it still misses the window between the sibling's own snapshot-read and its preflight write, and misses an at-venue position that exists but whose row hasn't flushed. The only fully-correct fix is the alternative the auditor also lists: ws_risk owning a single account-wide symbol-reservation table that all sleeves consult/claim before entry — a larger architectural change, not a one-line guard. (c) Given the LOW severity (transient, ws_risk-backstopped), the added latency/complexity on the entry hot path is a real cost that should be weighed; if implemented, it must (1) fail-closed on sibling-read error consistent with the existing shared-account fail-closed posture, (2) reuse the existing storage roots (DATA_ROOT/CONTINUOUS_DATA_ROOT already plumbed into ws_risk) rather than re-deriving them, and (3) ship the proposed regression test simulating a sibling pending order in the same symbol. As written ("and/or"), the fix is acceptable in intent but needs the fail-mode and hot-path-latency design work before it is safe to land.

title: Oldest-first eligibility ordering can let stale yesterday signals starve fresh today signals under the per-cycle cap
evidence: `eligible_ts` is sorted ASCENDING (line 848), and the candidate-collection loop breaks once `len(candidates) >= max_new_entries` (default 5) BEFORE the more-recent ts are reached (lines 928-931). So when many symbols fire on the older (yesterday) bar, the per-cycle cap is filled with yesterday's candidates and today's (fresher, possibly stronger) signals are never collected. The later dedup keeps most-recent per symbol but only among the already-collected set.
impact: alpha/execution: in busy regimes the sleeve preferentially fills slots with older signals over fresher ones, mildly diverging from the backtest's per-day processing and from the intended 'most-recent bar' priority.
proposed_fix: Iterate `eligible_ts` newest-first (descending) so fresher signals win the per-cycle cap, or collect all candidates then sort by signal_ts desc before truncating to max_new_entries.

verdict.reasoning:
The code mechanism is exactly as described. In `_select_long_entry_candidates` (liquidity_migration/long_native_event_demo.py:848), `eligible_ts` is sorted ASCENDING and the collection loop breaks once `len(candidates) >= max_new_entries` (lines 928-931), so when two distinct daily bars are eligible the older bar's candidates are collected first and can fill the per-cycle cap before the newer bar is examined.

I verified the preconditions actually occur:
- Daily bars (`daily_bars` in momentum_signals.py) carry day-end `ts_ms` exactly MS_PER_DAY (24h) apart, with `hourly_bars >= 20` filter, so today's PARTIAL bar appears in features after ~20:00 UTC while yesterday's bar (ts = today 00:00) is still within `SIGNAL_FRESHNESS_MS = 24h`. That ~20:00–24:00 UTC window is the only time two distinct ts pass the freshness filter (otherwise exactly one closed bar qualifies — the 24h spacing makes the two-bar overlap a thin boundary window, NOT the "last 2 closed daily bars" the comment at lines 846-847 implies).
- In that window yesterday's bar reliably emits via deadline fall-through (its 6h deadline = today 06:00 UTC, long past; `fc_sniper_skip_on_no_retrace=False`), so with `fc_top_volume_rank_max=10` FC can produce up to ~10 fall-through candidates and saturate the default `max_new_entries_per_cycle=5`. Today's partial bar only emits if `live_price <= retrace_threshold` immediately (its deadline is far in the future), so it is the loser when the cap is consumed.

If control had any positive MAR this delta goes NEGATIVE, so the cell looks WORSE and lands in 'descriptive', never investigation_positive. It cannot manufacture a promotion.

Zero-DD CONTROL path (the only over-statement direction: mar_control=0 so delta = full cell MAR) requires the baseline strategy (00_baseline) to have LITERALLY zero drawdown across the entire multi-year window — physically implausible for a real short strategy with hundreds of trades (test fixtures show 416/319 trades). title: r1_robustness block-bootstrap uses circular wrap-around indexing, stitching the last and first months of a 3-year series into the same resampled path
evidence: _block_bootstrap builds each resample by idx.extend((start+j)%n for j in range(block)) (lines 203-205), i.e. a circular block bootstrap. When start is near the end (e.g. start=n-1, block=3) the block wraps to months [n-1, 0, 1], concatenating December 2025 with January 2023 returns into one contiguous block. For a regime-conditional strategy (STATE.md: 2x MAR swing across eras) this artificially smooths the dependence structure across the regime boundary and can understate tail risk in the p5 estimate that the Tier-3 gate (block-bootstrap pooled MAR-delta p5>=0, STATE.md line 115) relies on.
impact: Mildly optimistic p5/tail estimates for a regime-dependent edge; the Tier-3 real-money gate consumes a p5 from this family of bootstrap (apply_decision_rule/r1). Bounded because Tier-3 also requires forward-demo OOS.
proposed_fix: Use a non-circular moving-block bootstrap (sample block starts only in [0, n-block]) or a stationary bootstrap, so blocks never straddle the series boundary; document the block unit (months) and that block=3 means 3 months per the Tier-3 spec.

Per-block straddle probability ≈ 2/n (~5.5%); with ~12 blocks per resampled path, roughly half of all paths contain at least one wrap block — a systematic property, not an edge case. For a documented regime-conditional edge (STATE.md: ~2x MAR swing across eras) this injects spurious cross-regime contiguity and mildly smooths the dependence structure, biasing the p5/tail estimate optimistically.

Crucially, the finding survives the "does it reach a real gate?" test. The p5 outputs are non-blocking at Tier-2 (correctly flagged; r1_robustness.py:399-401 says fragility diagnostics only set demo order). BUT STATE.md line 115 makes "Block-bootstrap pooled MAR-Δ p5 ≥ 0 (seed=0, block=3mo, n=5000)" an explicit Tier-3 REAL-MONEY gate, and this function's argparse defaults (seed=0, block=3, n_boot=5000 at lines 287-289) match that spec exactly. grep confirms this is the ONLY block-bootstrap implementation in the repo (apply_decision_rule.py has no bootstrap), and multiple pre-registrations cite r1_robustness's bootstrap p5 as the Tier-3 fragility input. Severity is correctly LOW: it is a genuine methodology defect (circular block bootstrap is the textbook-suboptimal choice vs moving-block/stationary for dependent series), but (a) magnitude is bounded — only ~2/n of draws straddle the boundary; (b) the bootstrap is one of several independent Tier-3 conditions (forward-demo OOS, DD<50%, residual Sharpe ≥0.3, stress, capacity), so it cannot by itself promote a bad strategy; (c) it is NOT in the PIT/look-ahead/survivorship correctness class and does not touch live trading, the demo ledger, or any production path — it is research-tooling refinement only.

Because it alters the seed=0 reproducibility baseline that STATE.md line 115 pins, the fix must ALSO update STATE.md line 115 and the module docstring (lines 13-15, 25) to read "moving-block (non-circular) 3-month blocks" — the auditor's fix already calls for documenting the block unit. title: residual_momentum is joined on a start-of-day key while the engine feature panel carries an end-of-day ts_ms — possible whole-signal day shift
evidence: _attach_residual_momentum builds `_rm_day = (ts_ms // ms_per_day) * ms_per_day` on BOTH the signal table and the feature panel (lines 334, 340) and left-joins on it. But the feature panel's `ts_ms` is the END-of-trading-day stamp (`day_start_ms + MS_PER_DAY`, volume_events_features.py:568) — flooring it with `// ms_per_day * ms_per_day` yields the day AFTER the trading day. If scripts/precompute_residual_momentum.py writes residual rows stamped at the trailing-residual day's own ts (start/close of day D) rather than D+1, the two `_rm_day` values describe different calendar days and the gate either drops the candidate (is_not_null filter) or attaches residual_momentum[D] to the wrong signal day. The precompute docstring says the live join 'floors now to TODAY's day_ts and exact-matches', implying a start-of-day key, which is NOT the engine panel's end-of-day key.
impact: alpha: a one-day misalignment between the residual-momentum selection gate and the volume-event panel would either silently empty the gated sleeve (no trades) or shift the selection signal a full day off the decision day — a correctness bug in the residual-momentum-gated profile that backtest-vs-live reconciliation may not catch if both sides share the same off-by-one.
proposed_fix: Make the join key explicit and identical in semantics on both sides: derive the trading day from the panel via trading_day_expr('ts_ms') (date of ts_ms-1ms) and from the residual table via its actual completion-day convention, then join on a string date, not a raw modulo floor. Add a test that asserts, for a known (symbol, day), the residual_momentum value attached to the event row equals sum(residual_return[D-7..D-1]).

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED via end-to-end trace of both join sides.

ENGINE-PANEL SIDE (left side of the join in _attach_residual_momentum, volume_events.py:340): the feature panel's ts_ms is the END-of-trading-day stamp. build_volume_features -> _daily_bars (volume_features.py:104) sets ts_ms = day_start_ms + aggregation_ms (= day_start_ms + MS_PER_DAY). Every aux-feature builder in volume_events_features.py uses the same convention ((ts_ms//MS_PER_DAY+1)*MS_PER_DAY at lines 184/226/270/343/374) and _daily_return_frame:568 confirms it. The code's own canonical helper trading_day_expr (_common.py:85) documents this: "ts_ms = day_start_ms + one period, so the trading day is the date of ts_ms - 1ms." So an event on trading day D carries ts_ms = day_start(D)+MS_PER_DAY = 00:00 UTC of D+1, and _rm_day = (ts_ms//ms_per_day)*ms_per_day = day_start(D+1).

RESIDUAL-TABLE SIDE (right side): the ONLY writer is scripts/precompute_residual_momentum.py, which writes resid['ts_ms'] straight from fit_factor_returns (risk_model.py:218-230). That ts_ms comes from build_factor_panel -> build_feature_panel, whose spine ts_ms is daily_klines.ts_ms from _aggregate_daily_klines (signal_harness.py:159,169) = min hourly ts_ms = day_start = 00:00 UTC of decision day D (the START-of-day grid; docstring at 251-254 + 707 say "ts_ms is the uniform 00:00-UTC daily grid"). build_feature_panel never shifts it +1 day (verified lines 863, 873-887). So the residual row for decision day D is keyed ts_ms = day_start(D), and its _rm_day = day_start(D). The residual_momentum value there is sum(residual_return[D-7..D-1]) (rolling_sum(7).shift(1)), the trailing momentum known strictly before D's close — the correct PIT value to gate a decision made at D's EOD.

MISMATCH: for the SAME trading day D, engine _rm_day = day_start(D+1) but residual-table _rm_day = day_start(D). I verified numerically (D=2026-05-26): engine -> 2026-05-27, residual row for that key -> decision day D+1 (2026-05-27). They are off by exactly +1 day and NEVER match for the same trading day. The left-join therefore attaches residual_momentum[D+1] = sum(residual_return[D-6..D]) to the day-D event — which (a) is the wrong selection day and (b) INCLUDES residual_return[D], the event day's own forward residual, i.e. a one-day LOOK-AHEAD leak into the gate.

LOAD-BEARING: the joined column directly drives survival in volume_events_filters.py:762-770 (is_not_null AND <= max). The gate activates whenever liquidity_migration_residual_momentum_max < 10.0 (volume_events.py:410). The existing test (test_..._gate_keeps_low_rmom) injects residual_momentum directly into the filter and only exercises the predicate — it does NOT exercise the join key, so the off-by-one is unguarded, exactly as the finding states.

SEVERITY = high (not critical): this is a methodology/correctness defect in the residual-momentum-gated EVENT-RESEARCH backtest path (the age-rmom-ff6-combined pre-reg experiment and any --liquidity-migration-residual-momentum-max cell). It corrupts the rmom-gate verdict with a look-ahead-contaminated, day-shifted selection. It is NOT in the deployed promoted SHORT profile (which doesn't set the gate) and NOT in the live CONTINUOUS sleeve (continuous_demo.py uses a separate day_ts join, not this code path), so no live ledger is mis-trading from this. Confined to research decisions, but those research decisions are exactly what gate promotion — hence high, not medium.
verdict.fix_notes:
The proposed fix is DIRECTIONALLY CORRECT but NOT a safe drop-in as literally phrased — apply with care.

Root cause: the two sides use DIFFERENT day conventions, so any fix must use the RIGHT (asymmetric) key on each side:
- Engine panel: trading day = date(ts_ms - 1ms) = trading_day_expr('ts_ms') (end-of-day stamp).
- Residual table: trading day = date(ts_ms) (start-of-day grid; its ts_ms already labels decision day D).

CORRECT FIX: join engine.trading_day_expr('ts_ms') == residual.date(ts_ms). Equivalently in the raw-modulo form: subtract MS_PER_DAY from the panel side before flooring (panel _rm_day = ((ts_ms - 1)//ms_per_day)*ms_per_day so day-D event maps to day_start(D)), leaving the residual side as-is.

PITFALL the verifier must flag: the finding's text says "derive the trading day from the panel via trading_day_expr AND from the residual table via its actual completion-day convention." That is right ONLY if the residual side is NOT also passed through trading_day_expr. Applying trading_day_expr to BOTH sides (the naive reading) shifts both by the same -1ms and PRESERVES the off-by-one — it would not fix anything. So the implementer must explicitly use trading_day_expr on the panel and plain date(ts_ms) on the residual table.

SIDE-EFFECT / non-no-op warning: this is a methodology correction, NOT a numerically-equivalent refactor. Fixing it WILL change which candidates survive the rmom gate and therefore changes the backtest output of every rmom-gated research cell (it currently silently selects the wrong, look-ahead day). Any prior age-rmom-ff6-combined results produced with the current code are tainted and must be re-run; a pre-registration receipt should accompany the re-run per AGENTS.md. It is safe for the live system (deployed/continuous paths don't use _attach_residual_momentum), so no live-trading risk from applying the fix.

REQUIRED REGRESSION TEST (the finding's suggestion is the right one): build a tiny klines + residual_momentum fixture for a known (symbol, D), run the engine join, and assert the residual_momentum attached to the event on trading day D equals the residual-table value for decision day D (i.e. sum(residual_return[D-7..D-1])), and explicitly that it does NOT equal day D+1's value. This locks the asymmetric key and would have caught the current bug.

title: TickerCache global staleness gate masks per-symbol stale prices feeding stop/exit decisions
evidence: TickerCache.is_stale() / seconds_since_last_event() are GLOBAL: any single symbol's ticker delta bumps _stats.last_event_monotonic, so the cache reports fresh as long as ANY symbol is pushing. _resolve_ticker_snapshot (event_demo.py:2191-2201) gates only on this global is_stale()/is_seeded(), then serves snapshot_list() wholesale. However the impact is narrower than "high". title: recover_from_disk sets _global_max_ts_ms from the flush file with no future-ts clamp, re-poisoning the evictor

title: OI/taker-flow 30-day clamp truncates the requested range, but the marker is written for the FULL range — permanent silent coverage gaps
evidence: get_open_interest_hist/get_taker_buy_sell_volume call _recent_history_start(start,end,days=30) which clamps the fetch start to max(start, end-30d+1, now-30d+1) — Binance only serves the last 30 days of these endpoints. So for a requested [start_ms,end_ms] spanning years, only the last ~30 days are returned. But _download_symbol_dataset (downloaders.py:565-581) calls fetch(effective_start_ms,end_ms) and then unconditionally writes _mark_complete for the FULL requested [start_ms,end_ms] range (the comment at 577-580 says it does this on purpose). The next refresh sees _marked_complete()==True for the full historical range and skips fetching forever, even though >99% of the historical window was never downloaded. The dataset permanently looks 'complete' to the marker layer while containing only a 30-day tail.
impact: alpha/data-integrity: binance_usdm_open_interest and binance_usdm_taker_flow_1h roots silently contain only ~30 days of history regardless of the requested span, and the marker system asserts they are fully covered. Any OI/flow feature on the Binance proxy root is computed on a near-empty history; a re-run will not self-heal because the marker gates the fetch.
proposed_fix: Either (a) record markers using the ACTUAL fetched/clamped range, not the requested range, for endpoints with provider history limits, or (b) for OI/taker-flow set the marker key to the clamped [effective_fetch_start, end] and never claim coverage older than the provider window. Surface the clamp in the printed log and in a per-dataset coverage manifest so consumers can detect the 30-day ceiling.

verdict.reasoning:
The mechanism is real and reachable via a concrete, documented production path. Verified each link:

1. CLAMP (binance.py:65-97, 206-209): get_open_interest_hist and get_taker_buy_sell_volume both call _recent_history_start(start,end,days=30), which returns max(start, end-30d+1, now-30d+1). For a multi-year requested span ending near now, this pins the actual fetch start to ~now-30d. Confirmed.

2. MARKER-VS-CLAMP (downloaders.py:561-581): On a first-ever download coverage_end is None, so effective_start_ms = start_ms (the full multi-year start) is passed to fetch() at line 565; the Binance client then clamps internally so only ~30d of rows land in storage. 3. The historical pre-30-day prefix is treated as covered forever; a same-start re-run never re-fetches it. Confirmed.

REACHABLE IN PRODUCTION: scripts/build_full_pit_binance.sh:25-26,65-70 runs `download-binance-proxy --start 2019-09-01 --end today --datasets ...,open_interest,...,taker_flow_1h`, a ~6.5-year span, and docs/data_roots.md calls the build "idempotent, resumable." Why MEDIUM, not HIGH:

- Coverage is independently auditable from ACTUAL ROWS, not markers: run_data_layer_audit / _load_coverage_snapshot (data_layer.py:90-164) reports real min/max row dates, and _dataset_notes (data_layer.py:548-549) already prints 'Binance REST history is recent-window only; archive separately for long tests'. title: Marker coverage claims full range even when fetch returned ZERO rows — empty/late-listing symbols are permanently marked complete and never refetched
evidence: _download_symbol_dataset writes _mark_complete(full requested range) unconditionally after write_dataset(frame,...), even when frame.height==0 (fetch returned [] — symbol not yet listed at start_ms, a transient empty REST response, or a provider hiccup that returned an empty list instead of raising). The marker file is non-empty (it stores an ISO timestamp at downloaders.py:664), so _marked_complete()==True on the next run and the range is skipped forever. A symbol that listed mid-window but returned [] on the first (pre-listing) refresh, or any symbol that momentarily returned an empty batch, is frozen as 'covered' with no rows.
impact: alpha/survivorship: missing per-symbol history that never self-heals on re-run is exactly the survivorship/coverage gap the methodology forbids; the PIT universe silently loses bars for affected symbols and the marker layer reports full coverage.
proposed_fix: Do not write the full-range completion marker when frame.height==0; either skip the marker (force retry next run) or write a distinct empty-result marker that is not treated as coverage. At minimum require rows>0 before claiming a never-before-covered range complete.

verdict.reasoning:
Traced the full triggering path and confirmed the bug. In `_download_symbol_dataset` (liquidity_migration/downloaders.py:565-585): `rows = fetch(effective_start_ms, end_ms)` → `frame = pl.DataFrame(rows, ...)` → `write_dataset(frame, ...)` → `_mark_complete(_marker_path(..., start_ms, end_ms, ...))` is called UNCONDITIONALLY, with no `frame.height` check. `write_dataset` short-circuits and writes ZERO rows on an empty frame (storage.py:340-342: `if df.is_empty(): path.mkdir(...); return path`), yet `_mark_complete` still writes a non-empty ISO timestamp (downloaders.py:664). On the next run, `_marked_complete` (downloaders.py:606-608) returns True for any marker with `st_size > 0`, so the exact `[start_ms, end_ms]` range is skipped forever (downloaders.py:543-545).

The empty-frame state is genuinely reachable: `BybitMarketData._get` (bybit.py:340-367) RAISES `BybitDataError` on any non-zero retCode and on transport errors after retries, so error states do NOT reach the frame as empty — they propagate and get skipped+retried at the symbol level. The ONLY way `frame.height==0` reaches `_mark_complete` is a `retCode==0` response with an empty `result.list`: (a) a genuine pre-listing window for a symbol requested from the single global `start_ms` (confirmed: `start_ms` is passed identically to every symbol via _download_rest_symbol_datasets, never clamped to per-symbol listing time), or (b) a successful-but-empty provider payload — a real, documented hiccup. `get_klines`/`_paged_time_range` return `[]` cleanly for empty batches.

The dangerous case is (b): a transient `retCode==0` empty payload for a window that DOES have data freezes that exact interior range with zero rows. The tail-extension path (downloaders.py:547-564) only re-fetches the extension BEYOND `end_ms`; it never re-fills an originally-empty interior, so the gap is permanent. This is precisely the survivorship/coverage gap docs/backtesting_errors_we_never_repeat.md forbids, and matches the repo's own audit-pattern lesson on empty-fetch-treated-as-authoritative. Case (a) freezes only windows that legitimately had no data and self-heals as end_ms advances past listing, so it's lower-risk. No existing test covers the empty-fetch path (tests all return non-empty rows or a fully-cached marker), confirming the behavior is unguarded.

Severity medium is correct: real data-integrity hazard in the forbidden survivorship class, but narrow trigger (needs a retCode==0 empty payload over a should-have-data window) and partially self-healing.
verdict.fix_notes: The proposed fix (require frame.height > 0 before writing the full-range completion marker) is correct and side-effect-free for the dangerous case. Recommended minimal change at downloaders.py:577-581 — guard the `_mark_complete(...)` call with `if frame.height > 0:`. Verified no downstream breakage: (1) both Bybit and Binance flows funnel through this single `_download_symbol_dataset` helper, so one guard fixes both venues; (2) `_assert_download_completeness` (binance_vision.py) does not depend on the `.done` coverage markers, so suppressing a marker won't trip a false completeness failure; (3) `write_dataset` already no-ops on empty frames, so no spurious partitions exist either way. Only side-effect: a genuinely pre-listing (legitimately empty) symbol re-fetches its full `[start_ms, end_ms]` window on every refresh until it lists — a bandwidth/time cost, NOT a correctness regression. To avoid that re-fetch thrash, a refined variant could either (a) write a ZERO-BYTE marker on empty (both `_marked_complete` and `_marker_coverage_end_ms` already skip `st_size == 0` markers, so it would be ignored for coverage but could be repurposed as a distinct empty-result record), or (b) only suppress the marker when coverage_end is None (never-before-covered range) so a transient empty over previously-covered data still forces a retry. The minimal `rows>0` guard the finding proposes is the safe baseline. Add a regression test asserting that an empty fetch leaves no full-range marker (and thus the next run re-fetches) — the test harness at tests/test_liquidity_migration_downloaders.py:521-590 already has the exact fixtures to extend.

title: Partial-exit legs never book realized PnL — multi-leg closes understate net_return (only the final leg is priced, at the reduced notional)
evidence: _partial_exit_trade_update keeps the trade status='open', reduces qty to remaining_qty, and records partial_exit_* metadata but writes NO gross/net_return for the closed leg (self-documented KNOWN LIMITATION at lines 406-414). impact: ledger/alpha: net_return understated for any trade that exits in multiple reduce-only legs (max-order-qty splits, partial market fills). Surfaces as pnl_gap_usdt in demo↔Bybit reconcile but is a real mis-statement in the ledger the forward-demo MAR is computed from; impact scales if max-order-qty splitting becomes common at size or on a real-money path.
proposed_fix: Book each partial leg's realized return at fill time: compute gross_trade_return for the filled_qty leg weighted by that leg's share of notional_weight, accumulate into a realized_return_acc field on the trade row, and have the final close add the remainder rather than overwrite. Add a test asserting a 2-leg close sums to the same net_return as a single full-qty close.
